{=taom_mcm_HideEmissaryWhenNoResource_hint}When on, the emissary option is hidden at settlements whose owner faction has no special resource. When off, the option still appears but is disabled with an explanatory hint.

{=taom_mcm_TournamentBetCapPerRound_hint}The most you may bet in each tournament round. 0 = unlimited (up to your purse); raise this slider for a bigger cap, or back to 0 to remove it. Roguery's Deep Pockets doubles any other value. Vanilla is 150. Default: 15,000. Saved values from before 2026-11-10 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

{=taom_mcm_TournamentRenownMultiplier_hint}Scales the renown a tournament winner earns (base: vanilla's 3 plus 1 per lord or hero in the field, times the winner's culture factor). 1.00 = as designed. Applies to every winner. Default: 1.00.

{=taom_mcm_TournamentInfluenceMultiplier_hint}Scales the influence a tournament winner earns in a town of their own kingdom (base: 2 plus 1 per 4 lords or heroes in the field, times the winner's culture factor). 1.00 = as designed. Default: 1.00.

{=taom_mcm_TournamentKeepEnemySidesOut_hint}A Free People's tournament seats no lord, wanderer or troop of the Shadow, and a tournament of the Shadow seats none of the Free Peoples; each is replaced by one of the town's own troops. A town's side is its owner's, so a captured town follows its conqueror, and a town held by a neutral realm bars nobody. Neutral lords and wanderers, the troops the town itself recruits, you and your clan always compete. Fewer lords in the field means a lesser prize. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableTidingsOfTheLists_hint}Adds an option to a town's training grounds menu: for a small fee the training master names the nearest towns holding a tournament now that are not at war with your realm. It marks nothing on the map. When off, the option is hidden. Single-player only. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableArmourAcquisition_hint}Markets and battle loot hand out light and medium armour freely. Heavy, elite and lord pieces are sold only where a town's armoury, its Barracks, is high enough; lord kit can also be forged there or earned piece by piece on the lord's gear ladder, whose last rung awards the named hero weapons; they are never sold or looted. Visit a town's armoury to upgrade a piece with metals. Takes effect from the next game load.
{=taom_mcm_EnableArmourLordEvent_hint}After a battle your side wins against an enemy lord, you may rarely find his household's lord harness among the spoils. Needs Armour Acquisition on.
{=taom_mcm_EnableVisitingArmourer_hint}Now and then a master armourer visits a town for a week, raising its armoury one level. Needs Armour Acquisition on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableCultureConversion_hint}When enabled, a town/castle (and its villages) conquered by a different culture gradually adopts the new owner's culture — producing their troops, militia, and identity. Disabling stops NEW conversions; already-converted settlements stay converted.
{=taom_mcm_CultureConversionHoldDays_hint}Days the new owner must hold a cross-culture fief before it converts. Lower = faster cultural takeover. Default: 1 (near-instant on capture).

{=taom_mcm_CultureConversionRequireStableLoyalty_hint}When enabled, a conquered fief only converts once its loyalty is high enough (configured in culture_conversion_config.json), so a city in unrest never flips. Default: off.

{=taom_mcm_CultureConversionReplaceNotables_hint}When enabled, conversion also replaces the settlement's notables with ones of the new culture (a Mordor-held Gondor town gets orc notables). Their workshops, alleys and caravans transfer to the newcomers; your relations with the old notables do not. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_CultureConversionReplaceGarrison_hint}When enabled, conversion re-mans the fief's garrison with the new culture's troops, matching tier, battlefield role and head count (a Gondor tier-4 archer becomes a Mordor tier-4 archer). Without this a fief taken by gift, barter or a king's decision keeps its old culture's garrison forever. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_CultureConversionReplaceMilitia_hint}When enabled, conversion also swaps the settlement's and its villages' existing militia to the new culture's militia troops. New militia already spawn in the new culture once the fief converts; this makes the standing militia catch up the same day instead of over many. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_CultureConversionReplaceGarrisonPlayerFiefs_hint}When disabled, the two swaps above never touch a fief your clan owns, so a garrison you stacked by hand survives the conversion. AI fiefs still swap, and your fief still changes culture. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_WarOfTheRingEnabled_hint}When enabled, a scripted war will escalate between Free Peoples and Dark Powers. This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.

{=taom_mcm_WarPhase1TriggerDay_hint}Days after campaign start when Isengard and Dunland attack Rohan. Default 30. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again. This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.

{=taom_mcm_WarPhase2TriggerDay_hint}Days after campaign start when all hostile kingdoms go to war and peace between hostile tiers is blocked. Default 44. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again. This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.
{=taom_mcm_TestMode_hint}Uses the short delays from war_of_the_ring.json (1/3 days) for rapid testing. Overrides Phase 1/2 days.

{=taom_mcm_MomentumEnabled_hint}Tracks Evil vs Good war progress from battles, sieges, raids, armies and relative strength. The war ends at the victory threshold only when Enable Victory (End the War) is on; that setting is off by default, so the war is endless. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_ShowWarOfTheRingMapMeter_hint}Shows the on-map War of the Ring slider once the full war begins. Click it for the detailed breakdown. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_MomentumVictoryEnabled_hint}When OFF (default) the War of the Ring is endless: momentum is tracked but no side ever wins. Turn ON to let a side win at the Victory Threshold (or by eliminating the other), which ends the war and makes peace. Default: off (endless). This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.
{=taom_mcm_MomentumVictoryThreshold_hint}Momentum lead one side needs to win the war outright. Default 500.
{=taom_mcm_MomentumParticipationMultiplier_hint}Momentum gains are multiplied by this when your party takes part in the event. Default 1.5.
{=taom_mcm_MomentumRequirePlayerForVictory_hint}When on, the war cannot end until you have fought in enough momentum events yourself. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_MomentumMinPlayerEvents_hint}How many battles/sieges you must take part in before either side can win. Default 5.

{=taom_mcm_WarRallyEnabled_hint}Gives AI kingdoms that have lost a large share of their towns and castles a small, temporary boost: a higher daily volunteer roll in their towns, castles and villages (empty recruit slots fill faster and waiting recruits are promoted sooner) and faster escapes for their captured lords. Never applies to a kingdom you rule, or to your own clan's settlements and lords; its lords in your prisons escape faster too. Takes effect at the next daily tick; turning it off removes every rally effect. Default on.

{=taom_mcm_WarEffectStrength_hint}Scales every War of the Ring catch-up and event effect (a higher daily volunteer roll, which fills recruit slots faster and promotes waiting recruits sooner; faster escapes of captured lords). 0 turns them off, 1 is the authored size, 2 doubles it. Default 1.

{=taom_mcm_EyeOfSauronEnabled_hint}When on, great deeds against the enemy draw a hunter: a Free player is hunted by one of the Nine with a host of Mordor (of Dol Guldur for its four wraiths), an Evil player by Glorfindel with a host of the Eldar. Only while your kingdom is at war with the hunter's. Single-player only. Default: on. This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.

{=taom_mcm_EyeThreshold_hint}Deed score that draws a hunt. A victory over an enemy kingdom in the field, a village raid or a forced levy scores 1, a sally or a battle outside a siege 2, a siege assault 3. Default 10.
{=taom_mcm_EyeHalfLifeDays_hint}Days for the deed score to fall by half. Default 30.
{=taom_mcm_EyeCooldownDays_hint}Days after a hunt ends before another can start. Default 60.
{=taom_mcm_HuntTimeoutDays_hint}Days a hunt lasts before the hunter gives up. Default 20.
{=taom_mcm_HunterSpeedMultiplier_hint}Once the hunter is within one and a half times your seeing range, it moves at least this many times your speed. Default 1.3.
{=taom_mcm_HunterStrengthRatio_hint}The hunter's host is filled to this many times your strength (your army's, when you lead one). Default 1.3.
{=taom_mcm_HunterMaxTroops_hint}The most men the hunter's party holds after its host is topped up. Default 250.
{=taom_mcm_HunterStepCap_hint}The farthest the hunter closes in one hour while out of your sight, in map units. Default 15.

{=taom_mcm_WarChronicleEnabled_hint}Runs the War Chronicle: lore events of the War of the Ring at set points, and the great sieges (Helm's Deep, Osgiliath, Minas Tirith and others) as timed windows whose result gives both sides small, temporary effects. Off stops new events and clears the army focus; the saved progress is kept. Default on.

{=taom_mcm_WarChronicleAnnouncements_hint}Shows a popup on the campaign map when a chronicle event happens, a siege window opens, or a siege is decided. Off keeps the events running silently. Default on.

{=taom_mcm_WarChronicleArmyFocus_hint}During a siege window, how much more the attackers' armies want to besiege the target and the defender's armies want to defend it once it is attacked. 1 turns the focus off. Needs AI Strategic Intelligence on. Default 1.4.
{=taom_mcm_EnableCustomTroopPower_hint}Enables configurable T7-T10 troop power values for battle simulation.
{=taom_mcm_OverrideVanillaTierPower_hint}If enabled, battle_balance_config.json TierPower values replace the vanilla formula for T1-T6.
{=taom_mcm_Tier7Power_hint}Base simulation power for T7 troops (vanilla formula extrapolation = 3.06).
{=taom_mcm_Tier8Power_hint}Base simulation power for T8 troops (vanilla formula extrapolation = 3.60).
{=taom_mcm_Tier9Power_hint}Base simulation power for T9 troops (vanilla formula extrapolation = 4.18).
{=taom_mcm_Tier10Power_hint}Base simulation power for T10 troops (vanilla formula extrapolation = 4.80).
{=taom_mcm_HeroMultiplier_hint}Multiplier applied to heroes in battle simulation. Vanilla = 1.5.
{=taom_mcm_MountedMultiplier_hint}Multiplier applied to mounted troops in battle simulation. Vanilla = 1.2.
{=taom_mcm_EnableCustomCasualtyRatios_hint}Enables configurable wound/kill ratios for battle simulation.
{=taom_mcm_PlayerBluntDamageChance_hint}Blunt (wound-only) damage chance in player battles. Vanilla = 0.30.
{=taom_mcm_AIBluntDamageChance_hint}Blunt damage chance in AI vs AI battles. Vanilla = 0.10.
{=taom_mcm_EnableCulturalSurvivalBonuses_hint}Applies the per-culture survival modifiers from battle_balance_config.json. A positive value means more of that culture's wounded survive.
{=taom_mcm_EnableSiegeDefenseEvents_hint}When enabled, you receive an event when a watched faction's settlement is besieged, with a timed window to help defend.
{=taom_mcm_SiegeDefenseResponseDays_hint}Number of in-game days to travel to a besieged settlement before the event expires.

{=taom_mcm_EnableArmyStrategicIntelligence_hint}When enabled, AI armies stick to their current target rather than re-optimising every 3 hours. Reduces army thrashing and improves siege follow-through.
{=taom_mcm_ArmyCommitmentMultiplier_hint}How strongly an army commits to its current target. 4.0 = the alternative must score 4x better before the army will divert. Vanilla implicit = 1.3.
{=taom_mcm_ArmyPriorityBoost_hint}Score multiplier applied to the first settlement in a faction's priority list. Decays linearly to 1.0 at the last entry. Affects Mordor, Isengard etc.

{=taom_mcm_EvilFactionAggressionScale_hint}Global multiplier applied to all per-faction strength inflation values from army_targeting.json. 1.0 = use JSON defaults. Raise to make evil factions siege even when outnumbered.

{=taom_mcm_ArmyBorderProximityFloor_hint}Minimum border-proximity score substituted for priority-list targets that vanilla rejects as out-of-range, and only for targets inside the march radius below. 0 = vanilla.
{=taom_mcm_EnableWarTheaters_hint}When enabled, kingdoms favour enemies on their own front. Gondor prefers Mordor and Isengard over far northern targets. Weighting only: no war is ever forbidden.

{=taom_mcm_ArmyBorderRescueRadius_hint}How far, in average town gaps, a priority-list target may be and still have its unreachable verdict overturned by the Border Proximity Floor above. Not a general distance penalty: the game already applies one of its own. 3.2 clears the widest real front on the map.
{=taom_mcm_ArmyDefenderPriority_hint}Score multiplier on defending one of your own settlements. Raise it if AI kingdoms keep besieging abroad while their own fiefs fall. 1.0 = vanilla.

{=taom_mcm_HoldCapturedForts_hint}When an AI army of a Free realm takes a town or castle by siege, it stays inside for about 22 hours (12 to 30: longer for a Calculating lord, shorter for a Valorous one) instead of the 10 the game gives. It leaves early if the fortress is besieged, its cohesion drops below 40 or it has less than a day of food, but holds are not saved: after loading a save a running hold cannot end early and runs to its end. Mordor's armies hold too; other Evil realms and (by default) Neutral ones keep rolling on. Single-player only. Needs AI Strategic Intelligence on. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_FastForwardMultiplier_hint}Speed multiplier for fast-forward: the map bar fast-forward button, and the fast-forward key (Space by default; rebind under Options > Keybindings > Campaign Map). Default: 4.

{=taom_mcm_ExtraFastForwardMultiplier_hint}Speed multiplier for extra fast-forward: the map bar Extra Fast Forward button (the fourth time button), and the extra fast-forward key (E by default, which is also Rotate Camera Right; rebind either under Options > Keybindings > Campaign Map). Never below the Fast Forward Multiplier. Default: 8.

{=taom_mcm_CtrlSpaceMultiplier_hint}Speed multiplier while holding Ctrl and the turbo key (Space by default; rebind under Options > Keybindings > Campaign Map). Releases back to prior speed on key-up. Default: 16.
{=taom_mcm_EnableSiegeDismount_hint}Master toggle for the siege auto-dismount feature. When off, sieges behave vanilla (mount stays equipped).

{=taom_mcm_SiegeMountBehavior_hint}0 = Vanilla (no change). 1 = RESERVED (currently equivalent to Vanilla — full implementation deferred; would spawn the horse on the map separately). 2 = Mount moves to inventory for siege duration; player must re-equip manually after. 3 = Mount moves to inventory and is auto-restored after siege ends. Default: 3.
{=taom_mcm_SiegeDismountDebug_hint}Show diagnostic [SiegeDismount] messages on the in-game HUD. Off = file log only.

{=taom_mcm_EnableSiegeTroopPicker_hint}Before an assault, or before defending a siege, open the 'Manage Troops' screen the lord's hall fight uses and choose who fights. By default, trolls start unticked; tick them to bring them. Troops you leave out take no part in the battle and suffer no losses in it. Takes effect from the next assault. As defender, pressing Escape in the battle surrenders the siege and everyone with it, reserves included. When off, every troop fights as in vanilla. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_EnableCreatureSiegeRole}Trolls Stay Off Siege Ladders, Towers and Walls

{=taom_mcm_EnableCreatureSiegeRole_hint}In a wall battle, trolls never use siege ladders, towers or siege engines. Attacking trolls break the gate down instead, and defending trolls hold the ground behind it and stay off the walls while the AI commands them; a formation you give orders to obeys them. Takes effect from the next battle. When off, trolls behave as in vanilla. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_EnableSiegePropDiagnostics_hint}Log why rock piles and arrow barrels can or cannot be used in the current mission. Diagnostic only — changes no gameplay. Off by default.
{=taom_mcm_SiegePropDiagnosticsVerbose_hint}Log every prop, including working ones. Off = log only props that are unusable, plus the summary.

{=taom_mcm_EnableHowdahDiagnostics_hint}Write the war elephant howdah's and the mumakil war tower's diagnostics to the TAOM log: why a rider did or did not get a howdah, each platform's layout and floor clearance over its beast, a status line every 5 seconds per platform (beast speed against its walking speed, platform drift, how many archers are seated and how many can reach a target) and a battle summary. Diagnostic only, changes no gameplay. On by default while the platforms are being tested.

{=taom_mcm_EnableEnlistment_hint}Serve as a soldier in a lord's party — enlist, take a rank, draw wages, follow the column into battle. Turn OFF to remove the feature: the option to enlist disappears, and if you are already serving you are released honourably (you keep your pay and your gear) rather than being left parked on the map. Takes effect within three in-game hours (in a battle, once it ends); no restart. Default ON.

{=taom_mcm_OfferLeaveOnArrival_hint}When your company stops at a town, castle or village, ask whether you want a few hours to yourself. The popup exists because the wait menu runs at full speed: a lord's stop is a few campaign hours, which is about two real seconds, and the 'Take leave in the settlement' menu option appears and vanishes inside it. Turn this off and that menu option still works. Takes effect immediately; no restart. Default ON.

{=taom_mcm_EnableEnlistmentTrace_hint}Off by default: turn it on to record the routine enlistment trace ([EnlistDiag] TICK, SYNC ok, PARK ok, RESTORE ok) in the TAOM debug log when you are reproducing an enlistment problem for a bug report. It is roughly ten times the volume of the ordinary enlistment log, so turn it off again afterwards. Real faults are always logged regardless of this setting, so [EnlistDiag] lines still appear for them when it is off. Takes effect immediately; no restart.

{=taom_mcm_EnableFieldCommission_hint}Soldiers who do the killing in a hard-won battle can be promoted into named companions. Turn OFF to stop it entirely: no merit is earned, no promotion is ever offered. Companions you already promoted stay exactly as they are, and banked merit is kept in case you turn it back on. Takes effect immediately; no restart. Default ON.

{=taom_mcm_FieldCommissionOffersPerBattle_hint}The most promotion prompts a single won battle may raise. Each prompt pauses the game, so a large number after a large battle means a long queue of dialogs. Merit above the cap is not lost — it carries to the next battle. Default: 2. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

{=taom_mcm_FieldCommissionRatioThreshold_hint}How outnumbered you must be for a battle to count. Your party's healthy troops divided by the whole enemy side must come in UNDER this. 1.00 = only fights where you are outnumbered; higher = easier fights still earn merit. Default: 1.30.
{=taom_mcm_FieldCommissionMeritPerKill_hint}Merit a troop type banks for each enemy its soldiers kill in a qualifying battle. Higher = faster promotions. Default: 1.

{=taom_mcm_FieldCommissionMeritToPromote_hint}Merit a troop type must bank before it earns a promotion offer. Note merit is pooled per troop TYPE, not per soldier — a large stack of one type reaches the bar faster than a small one. Higher = rarer promotions. Default: 32. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

{=taom_mcm_FieldCommissionRetainerAllowance_hint}How many promoted companions you may take beyond your clan tier's companion limit. 0 = the limit is strict and an offer waits until you have room. Default: 0.

{=taom_mcm_EnableFieldCommissionDiagnostics_hint}Write a detailed [FieldCommission] trace to the TAOM debug log — which battles counted, which troops earned merit, which offers were raised, and every completed promotion. Turn this on before reproducing a promotion problem so the log you send answers it. Real faults are logged regardless of this setting. Off by default.

{=taom_mcm_EnableMessengers_hint}Send paid messengers to heroes. The price grows with distance. They travel for several days and trigger a conversation on arrival. Disable to grey out the encyclopedia button and stop the dialog line.

{=taom_mcm_MessengerGoldCost_hint}Denar price of the shortest trip. The price grows with the distance to the target, and is higher again when the target is at war with you, when you have never met them, and when they sit in a besieged town or castle. A stranger costs more but is never refused. The per-day rate and the multipliers live in messenger_config.json.
{=taom_mcm_MessengerTravelDays_hint}In-game days a messenger spends in transit before arriving at the target. Speed scales to map size. The days also scale the price.
{=taom_mcm_MessengerAccidents_hint}Random ambush chance during travel. The base hourly probability lives in messenger_config.json (default 0.2%).

{=taom_mcm_EnableMixedFormations_hint}Master toggle. When off, formations use vanilla positioning. When on, formations with mixed melee + ranged units are reordered per the chosen layout while holding position.

{=taom_mcm_MixedFormationsDefaultLayout_hint}Default layout auto-applied to mixed-class formations (>=5 minority units AND >=20% minority share AND >=10 total units). 0=Infantry front + Ranged back. 1=Ranged front + Infantry back. 2=Ranged on the wings, Infantry in the center. 3=Checkerboard. Default: 0.

{=taom_mcm_MixedFormationsCycleHotkey_hint}Bannerlord InputKey name. Pressing this while a formation is selected cycles its layout to the next; pressing while no formation is selected cycles all formations. Default: L.
{=taom_mcm_MixedFormationsDebug_hint}Writes two diagnostic lines, the auto-assigned default layout and the cycled layout, to the TAOM log file. Nothing is shown on the HUD.

{=taom_mcm_EnableFiefManagement_hint}Master toggle. When off, the F6 hotkey and the Fiefs button on the map bar are inert and the carousel options are disabled. Effective immediately at runtime. Default: true.

{=taom_mcm_AllowRemoteBuildingQueue_hint}When on, you can manage any owned fief from anywhere via F6 or the Fiefs button on the map bar. When off, the Manage option is disabled unless you are physically at the selected fief. Default: true.
{=taom_mcm_FiefManagementDebug_hint}Write diagnostic [FiefManagement] messages to the TAOM file log. Off = silent.

{=taom_mcm_EnablePosternGate_hint}A Postern Gate (a Hidden Door, Culvert, Sally Port, Hidden Way or Bolt-Hole, by culture) in a besieged fief cuts the troops lost breaking into or out of the siege there: by default 50, 67 and 75 percent by building level (postern_gate.json). When off, the building still exists but the cut does not apply. Takes effect at the next break-in or break-out. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableFromTheAshes_hint}Lets your company rebuild a looted village of your own realm from the village menu, and lend its labour to a construction project in a fief you own from the keep menu (from_the_ashes.json holds the hours, labour and materials). When off, those two options are hidden; a job already under way still finishes or stops normally. Single-player only. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableReevesLedger_hint}On the town management window: the fief's name as the title, a Profit row with a daily breakdown, a Patrol row for towns, and tooltips on the stash and prison icons. When off, the title, rows and icons are vanilla; the step buttons have their own switch. Applies the next time the window opens. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableReserveSteps_hint}Adds a button beside the reserve's plus button to put gold into the reserve in one click, and one to take a step back out, refunded in full with no penalty. Single-player only. Applies the next time the window opens. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableNamegiving_hint}Lets the ruler of your realm rename its towns, castles and villages from the Fiefs tab of the kingdom screen for influence, and lets four fiefs take an older or darker name while the matching side holds them. A name you chose is never overwritten. Single-player only. Switching it off gives those fiefs their map names back; a name you chose stays. The button follows the next time the kingdom screen opens; the older names change at the next capture, load or change of realm. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableWatchSilver_hint}Lets you talk to the governor of a town or castle your clan owns, inside that fief, and pay silver to the watch to raise its loyalty. Each offer shows its price, and there is a ceiling on how far silver can raise loyalty. When off, the line is hidden. Single-player only. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableHallSeats_hint}A lord's hall shows only as many lords as it has places for, instead of packing every lord in the town or castle onto one spot. The settlement's owner, the ruler, the governor, your own clan, quest givers and the lord you open a conversation with from the town menu always appear; the other places go to the owner's clan first, then clan leaders, then the strongest clans. The lords left out are still in the settlement. Takes effect from the next visit. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_EnableQuickActions_hint}Master toggle. When off, inventory 'Sell All' uses vanilla. When on, it opens a 4-option menu.
{=taom_mcm_EnableInventorySearch_hint}Inventory search box visibility; persists per save and reconciles to MCM each campaign frame.
{=taom_mcm_DamagedQualityDropdown_hint}Items at or below this damage level are sold. Pristine = unused (sentinel). Default: Moderate (-20%).
{=taom_mcm_DamagedThreshold_hint}Custom threshold. Only used when 'Use Custom Threshold' is on. Default: -0.20.
{=taom_mcm_ExcludeDamagedHorses_hint}Skip horses/mounts when selling damaged. Default: true.
{=taom_mcm_LowValueThreshold_hint}Items at or below this denars value are sold. Default: 100.
{=taom_mcm_QuickActionsShowConfirmation_hint}Ask for confirmation before bulk-selling. Default: true.
{=taom_mcm_QuickActionsPlaySounds_hint}Play 'event:/ui/transfer' chime after each batch action. Default: true.
{=taom_mcm_QuickActionsDebug_hint}Show diagnostic [QuickActions] HUD messages. Off = file log only.
{=taom_mcm_EnableEquipmentPresets_hint}Master toggle. When off, the Presets overlay is not added to the inventory screen and existing presets are inert (preserved in save).
{=taom_mcm_EquipPresetsDebug_hint}Show diagnostic [EquipPresets] messages on the in-game HUD. Off = file log only.

{=taom_mcm_EnableSmartCavalryCharge_hint}Master toggle. When off, cavalry uses vanilla charge logic. When on, the player's cavalry formations execute coordinated line charges with passthrough + reform behavior. Default OFF while war-elephant interaction is being tuned. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.
{=taom_mcm_SmartCavalryAvoidFriendlies_hint}When charging, cavalry will reroute around friendly infantry on the charge line. Off = vanilla collision behavior (cavalry trample friendly).

{=taom_mcm_SmartCavalryChargeStrictness_hint}How close riders must be to their slots before the line charges, and before a reform counts as done: the average rider may be 10 m off at 0, 4.4 m at the 0.7 default, 2 m at 1. Max Line-Up Seconds launches the charge regardless when it runs out.
{=taom_mcm_SmartCavalryReformDistance_hint}Meters past the target before cavalry reforms a new line. Larger = wider passthrough sweep. Default 25.
{=taom_mcm_SmartCavalryLineSpacing_hint}Multiplier on default unit spacing during line formation. 1.0 = vanilla. 1.2 (default) = slightly wider line for cleaner charge.
{=taom_mcm_SmartCavalryMaxLineUpSeconds_hint}Longest the cavalry spend lining up before they charge anyway, and before they re-charge after a reform. Lower is snappier with a looser line. Default 4.
{=taom_mcm_SmartCavalryDebug_hint}Also write every intercepted charge order and the state it produced to the TAOM log file. State transitions are logged regardless. Nothing is drawn on the HUD.

{=taom_mcm_EnableCultureDoctrine_hint}Each culture's AI fights field battles with its own doctrine: Dwarves hold a shield wall on the high ground, Elves ring their archers with infantry, Rohan leads with cavalry, Mordor and Gundabad mass their infantry. Replaces the tactic list the engine's team AI chooses from; the AI still picks by weight every 5 seconds. Applies from the NEXT battle (the list cannot change once a battle has started). Your own orders are never touched; when you delegate command (F6) your army fights with its culture's doctrine. Off by default until the in-game A/B passes; tuning lives in ModuleData/culture_doctrine/culture_doctrines.json, which reloads on game restart only.

{=taom_mcm_CultureDoctrineDebug_hint}Write a [Doctrine] status line to the TAOM log every 5 seconds of battle time: each team's current tactic and every formation's active behaviour and arrangement. The console command taom.tactic_status prints the same line on demand. Nothing is drawn on the HUD.

{=taom_mcm_CultureDoctrineMorale_hint}Each culture's soldiers hold under fear their own way: Dwarves, Elves, Isengard, Gundabad and Dol Guldur never rout (pride, or a hatred too great), the free peoples of Rohan, Gondor and Dale and the men of the East and South break as vanilla does, and every culture carries a bravery offset on its starting morale. Needs Enable Culture Doctrine. Applies from the next battle; tuning in culture_doctrines.json.

{=taom_mcm_CultureDoctrineAggression_hint}Each culture's soldiers fight the melee their own way: orcs attack on sight and rarely cover with a shield, Dwarves and Gondor raise shields and hold, Elves shoot straighter, Rohan commits to a charge from further out. Multiplies the engine's per-soldier AI decision values after skill has set them. Needs Enable Culture Doctrine. Applies to soldiers spawned from the next battle; tuning in culture_doctrines.json.

{=taom_mcm_CultureDoctrineHorseStand_hint}Dwarves, Isengard and Dale, defending outnumbered against an army of mostly horse, stand where horse cannot ride them down: a choke point, a forest, a slope, or where they are. Where the riders sit on ordinary horses, the cavalry dismount and join the shield wall with polearms ready. The AI sides only; your own army is never touched. Needs Enable Culture Doctrine. Applies from the next battle; tuning in culture_doctrines.json.

{=taom_mcm_EnableDeadMountDespawn_hint}Remove killed horses, wargs and other mounts a few seconds after they die instead of leaving them on the field. A mount is a full agent with a skeleton and a live ragdoll, so a cavalry battle piles up corpses that cost frame time and do nothing. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs only; towns, training grounds and tournaments keep their bodies. Side effect: freeing agent slots lets reinforcements arrive slightly sooner than vanilla.

{=taom_mcm_DeadMountDespawnDelaySeconds_hint}Seconds between a mount's death and its fade. Default 5. Below 3 the corpse pops while the death animation is still playing, so values outside 3-30 fall back to 5.

{=taom_mcm_EnableBattleCorpseCleanup_hint}Fade fallen soldiers after a set time and cap how many bodies a battle keeps, whatever your Number of Corpses option says. The engine walks its whole corpse list every frame, and players reported mid-battle freezes at high corpse settings. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs only; towns, training grounds and hideouts keep their bodies. Never raises your own Number of Corpses option.

{=taom_mcm_BattleCorpseFadeSeconds_hint}Seconds a body stays on the field, counted from when it settles, before it fades. Default 60. The engine's own default is an hour, so without this a body only goes when the corpse cap pushes it out. Values outside 10-300 fall back to 60.
{=taom_mcm_BattleCorpseCap_hint}Most bodies a battle keeps at once; the oldest fade first. Default 25, the vanilla Low setting. If your own Number of Corpses option is lower, yours is used.

{=taom_mcm_ShowBattleSettingsAdvice_hint}On the first main menu after the game starts, offer to lower Number of Ragdolls to 5 and Number of Corpses to Low when yours are higher. Nothing changes unless you click Apply.

{=taom_mcm_ApplyRecommendedBattleSettingsAction_hint}Lower Number of Ragdolls to 5 and Number of Corpses to Low (25) in your game options now. A setting already lower is kept. Change them back at any time in Options, Performance.
{=taom_mcm_EnableCompanionRoleTooltips_hint}Append detected combat role (e.g., [BOW], [INF]) to companion/troop tooltips on the party screen.
{=taom_mcm_EnableOOBRoleDisplay_hint}Show role indicators on hero items in the Order of Battle screen.
{=taom_mcm_CompanionRolesDebug_hint}Show diagnostic [CompanionRoles] messages on the in-game HUD.

{=taom_mcm_EnableOobFormationPresets_hint}Presets save and load the formation types, captains and hero troops of the Order of Battle, per campaign. Off by default until it is checked in game; opt in to try it. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.
{=taom_mcm_MaxFormationPresets_hint}Maximum saved formation presets per campaign. Save attempts beyond this limit are refused with a warning. Default: 10.

{=taom_mcm_ShowBattleActionBar_hint}Parked: show a bar of stance buttons during field battles. The buttons record a stance but do not change formation behavior yet, and they can be clicked only while a menu shows the cursor (for example Esc). Default: off.
{=taom_mcm_CancelStanceOnMove_hint}Auto-clear stance when the formation receives a movement order.
{=taom_mcm_EnableVolleyFire_hint}Include 'Volley Fire' as a ranged action option.

{=taom_mcm_EnableBanditScaling_hint}Master toggle. When off, hideout density + bandit party sizes use vanilla values. When on, both scale with PlayerProgress (0.0 new campaign -> 1.0 endgame) per the curves below. Turning it off restores vanilla's live numbers at once (including its 2-party minimum for a camp to count as infested) and stops scaling future spawns; it deletes no bandit party already on the map and culls no hideout above the cap, so a swamped campaign thins only as they are cleared.

{=taom_mcm_BanditDensityCurve_hint}Multiplier on hideout count + parties-per-hideout at PlayerProgress=1.0. Curve: 1 + curve * progress. 0 = vanilla density throughout. 1.5 (default) = up to 2.5x density in endgame. Both caps below bind first.

{=taom_mcm_BanditPartySizeCurve_hint}Multiplier on bandit party troop counts at PlayerProgress=1.0. Vanilla already scales 0.4 -> 1.2; this is a final multiplier on top. 1.5 (default) = up to 2.5x bandit party sizes in endgame. Each troop stack is capped at its party template's max_value, which binds before 2.5x is reached.

{=taom_mcm_BanditBossFightCurve_hint}Multiplier on the FIRST fight's troop count inside hideouts at PlayerProgress=1.0. 1.5 (default) = up to 2.5x bandits in the camp-clearing phase of a hideout assault in endgame. The boss fight is not scaled: it is exactly the boss plus Hideout Boss Bodyguards below.
{=taom_mcm_BanditMaxHideoutsPerFaction_hint}Hard cap on hideouts per bandit faction regardless of scaling curve. Vanilla = 9. Default: 100 (effectively the physical hideout count per faction).

{=taom_mcm_BanditPartiesPerHideoutCap_hint}Hard cap on bandit parties per hideout regardless of scaling curve. Vanilla = 3, which is also the floor: a cap at or below 3 pins the value at vanilla and the Density Curve cannot move it. Default: 6. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

{=taom_mcm_BanditStartingHideoutsPerFaction_hint}Hideouts each bandit faction starts with on a NEW campaign; read once at world-gen, so changing it does nothing to a campaign already in progress. TAOM has 8 bandit factions, so this is a per-faction target, x8 on the map, bounded by each faction's physical hideout count (three have only 10). Vanilla = 7. Default: 7. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

{=taom_mcm_BanditHideoutBossBodyguards_hint}Soldiers standing with the hideout boss in the final fight, on both the daytime assault and the night sneak-in. The fight is exactly the boss plus this many (0 = the boss alone), whether you take the duel or fight them all; the rest of the camp is cleared in the first phase. Applies with Enable Bandit Scaling off too. Vanilla fields 5 to 10 with the boss. Default: 4.

{=taom_mcm_EnableAlignmentRecruitment_hint}When enabled, a recruiter cannot recruit volunteers at a settlement controlled by an opposed-alignment kingdom (Free vs Evil). Alignment comes from execution/alignment.json, keyed by the kingdom you serve. Neutral factions (Umbar etc.) never block. When off, recruitment is vanilla. This is the default for new campaigns. With the Alignment rules start option on Standard, a campaign follows this switch live; Strict or Relaxed fixes all four alignment switches for that campaign. Older saves follow this setting.

{=taom_mcm_AlignmentRecruitmentGoodRejectsEvilOnly_hint}When ON, only a Free-aligned recruiter is blocked from Evil-controlled settlements; Evil recruiters may recruit anywhere, and Alignment Desertion then removes no Free troops from Evil lords or their garrisons at all, not only the ones they recruit. When OFF (default), the block is symmetric: Free and Evil each refuse the other, and opposed troops desert either way.

{=taom_mcm_EnableAlignmentRecruitmentPlayer_hint}When ON (default), YOU are blocked from recruiting in opposed-alignment settlements. When OFF, you may recruit anyone regardless of alignment (AI lords are still gated if 'Apply To AI Lords' is on). The master 'Enable Recruitment Alignment Block' toggle off disables the whole feature for everyone.

{=taom_mcm_EnableAlignmentRecruitmentAi_hint}When ON (default), AI lords are also blocked from recruiting in opposed-alignment settlements. When OFF, AI recruits freely (you are still gated if 'Apply To Player' is on).

{=taom_mcm_EnableMarriageAlignment_hint}When enabled, a Free-aligned hero cannot marry an Evil-aligned one (no Gondorian weds an orc). Alignment comes from execution/alignment.json, keyed by the hero's CULTURE. Neutral cultures (Khand, Umbar, Shaghana, Abanissa) marry anyone; Dunland is Evil. When off, marriage is vanilla. This is the default for new campaigns. With the Alignment rules start option on Standard, a campaign follows this switch live; Strict or Relaxed fixes all four alignment switches for that campaign. Older saves follow this setting.

{=taom_mcm_EnableMarriageAlignmentPlayer_hint}When ON (default), YOUR clan is also held to the rule — you and your siblings/children cannot marry across the Free/Evil line. When OFF, the player clan marries freely (AI lords are still gated if 'Apply To AI Lords' is on).

{=taom_mcm_EnableMarriageAlignmentAi_hint}When ON (default), AI lords are blocked from marrying across the Free/Evil line. When OFF, AI marries freely (you are still gated if 'Apply To Player' is on).

{=taom_mcm_MarriageAlignmentSteerAiSearch_hint}When ON (default), AI lords look for a partner among compatible clans instead of drawing uniformly from every clan in the world. Vanilla's draw wastes the day whenever it lands on a blocked clan, which would make Free factions (Gondor, Rohan, Dale) marry far less often and run short of heirs. Turn OFF to keep the block but restore vanilla's draw.

{=taom_mcm_EnableWandererAllegiance_hint}When enabled, a wanderer will not take service across the Free/Evil line: Free-culture wanderers (Gondor, Rohan, the Elves, Erebor and the rest) refuse a player who serves Sauron, and Evil-culture wanderers refuse a player on the Free side. Your side is the kingdom you serve (execution/alignment.json), falling back to your clan's culture when you serve no kingdom. Neutral cultures serve anyone and a Neutral player is refused by nobody. Companions already in your clan are never affected. When off, hiring is vanilla.

{=taom_mcm_WandererAllegianceScope_hint}All wanderers (default): every wanderer, by culture. Named companions only: just the lore characters from named_companions.xml (Aragorn, Legolas, Gimli and the rest); generic tavern wanderers hire as in vanilla.

{=taom_mcm_EnableHardQuestions_hint}When enabled, a lord held prisoner by your clan (in your party or in one of your settlements) can be questioned about his clan's or kingdom's lands, for a bribe or by force, and stripped of his arms and armour. Force and stripping cost relation, Honor and Mercy, and stripping costs renown. Each topic works once per captivity. When off, those conversation options do not appear.

{=taom_mcm_EnableTroopGifts_hint}When enabled, a conversation with a lord who leads a party offers a line to gift him troops through a donate-style party screen. The lord must not be in your clan or kingdom, not at war with you, and not on the opposite side of the Free/Evil divide (a Neutral lord may receive). Troops move from you to him only. The gift is paid by Bonds of Battle's hand-over rule (half the influence the gift is worth, at most 10 relation a day per relation owner), so the relation needs Bonds of Battle and its Troop Gifts Win Lords' Favour switch on; with either off the gift is still accepted but earns nothing. When off, the line does not appear.

{=taom_mcm_EnableDomainReveal_hint}When enabled, you can ask a free lord about his clan's holdings. A lord who knows you well enough names them and they are marked on your map; a lord who does not refuses, and a lord whose clan holds nothing says so, each at a small cost in relation. Lords at war with you and your own clan never answer. When off, the line does not appear.

{=taom_mcm_EnableNotableServices_hint}When enabled, a notable of the settlement you stand in (an artisan, gang leader, merchant, rural notable or headman, but not a preacher) offers three lines in conversation: give men to the settlement (troops raise its militia, prisoners its hearth in a village or its prosperity in a town; a castle takes troops only), pay to be introduced to the other notables there, and pay to have the nearest towns and castles marked on your map. Single player only; all three lines are hidden during a messenger conversation. At war with the settlement's realm only the gift line is hidden: the introduction still works and the holds question is refused. The gift line is also hidden while a party screen is open or when you hold no regular troop or prisoner. Amounts are in notable_services.json. When off, none of the lines appear. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableBanditGreetings_hint}When enabled, if you attack on land a bandit party you have not dealt with before and it belongs to one of the eight talking clans (Dunlending, Rhun, Haradrim, Gundabad, Umbar, Gondor deserters, Blacklocks, Mirkwood Stalkers), there is a one in four chance that it greets you in its own words, and your ultimatum is vanilla's reply to that kind of greeting. With Encounter Lines also on, these clans greet you in a line chosen by your people and your side on half of these meetings, and keep vanilla's greeting on the other quarter. Feral Orcs and looters, which have no greetings of their own, greet you that way on three meetings in four. Spiders and wild trolls are unchanged. Applies to the next bandit conversation. Text only: nothing else about the encounter changes. When off, every greeting is vanilla's. The lines bandits use when they rob you are separate data; with Encounter Lines on, half of these robberies use its lines instead. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableEncounterLines_hint}When enabled, lords you meet on the map speak in the voice of their people and by who you are to them: their liege, an ally, a rival, a foe, or one of their own. Caravans and villagers greet you this way half of the time on a first meeting on land, and speak their own words when they surrender to a robbery. Bandit clans rob you with their own threats, and a hideout boss challenges you in the clan's own words. Bandit greetings when you attack a bandit party also need Enable Bandit Clan Greetings (World/Bandit Voices) on. Lords in your clan, companions, wanderers and notables keep vanilla's lines, and so do lords you speak to inside a settlement; the hideout boss still speaks the clan's own words. Applies to the next conversation. Text only: nothing else about the encounter changes, but TAOM's lines are not voiced, so a line that replaces a voiced vanilla line is silent. When off, every line is vanilla's. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableInnRounds_hint}When enabled, the tavern keeper of a town offers three more lines: stand a round for your whole party (morale and a little Charm experience), stand a round for everyone in the tavern (renown and a little Charm experience), and pay to have the nearest towns and castles marked on your map. A round costs the town's price for the local drink for each head, capped, and the gold goes to the town. At most a few rounds a day, set in inn_rounds.json. Single player only; the lines are hidden during a messenger conversation. The map question is refused while the town's realm is at war with yours or its owner does not know you well enough. When off, none of the lines appear. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_InnRoundsMoraleScale_hint}Multiplies the morale a party round gives (20 to 40 before the scale, set in inn_rounds.json). 0 gives none; the party's morale never goes past 100. Between 0 and 3. Default: 1.
{=taom_mcm_InnRoundsRenownScale_hint}Multiplies the renown a house round gives (1 to 3 before the scale, set in inn_rounds.json), rounded to a whole number. 0 gives none. Between 0 and 3. Default: 1.

{=taom_mcm_EnablePrisonerRecruitmentWaiver_hint}When enabled (default), recruiting a prisoner of your own faction or your own side of the war costs no morale — an Isengard captor loses nothing taking on Mordor, Gundabad or Dunland troops, since all serve Sauron. Alignment comes from execution/alignment.json. Neutral factions (Khand, Umbar) only waive their own culture, not each other. When off, prisoner morale is vanilla (-1 per troop, -2 per bandit).

{=taom_mcm_EnablePrisonerRecruitmentWaiverPlayer_hint}When ON (default), YOU pay no morale for same-side prisoners. When OFF, you pay the vanilla cost (AI lords still get the waiver if 'Apply To AI Lords' is on).

{=taom_mcm_EnablePrisonerRecruitmentWaiverAi_hint}When ON (default), AI lords also pay no morale for same-side prisoners, so allied factions absorb each other's captured troops more readily. When OFF, only you benefit (if 'Apply To Player' is on).

{=taom_mcm_EnableNavalTravel_hint}Currently DISABLED — the map's navmesh isn't set up for naval travel yet, so this feature is parked in code and this toggle has no effect for now. (When re-enabled: parties sail across water on the campaign map — the engine's native naval travel, unlocked without the Naval DLC.)

{=taom_mcm_NavalTravelApplyToPlayer_hint}When ON (default), YOUR party can sail. When OFF, you stay land-bound (AI still sails if 'Apply To AI Lords' is on). The master 'Enable Naval Travel' toggle off disables sailing for everyone.
{=taom_mcm_NavalTravelApplyToAi_hint}When ON (default), AI lords' parties can also sail. When OFF, only the player sails and AI stays on land — the conservative option if AI naval routing looks odd.

{=taom_mcm_EnableAlignmentDesertion_hint}When enabled, troops whose culture is opposed in alignment to their lord (Free vs Evil) desert each day: an Evil lord sheds Good troops and a Good lord sheds Evil troops. Alignment comes from execution/alignment.json. Neutral cultures (Umbar etc.) never desert. Troops that would desert cannot be recruited from prisoners, notables' volunteers or by garrison auto-recruit (tavern mercenaries are not checked). With Recruitment Alignment on and its 'Only Good Rejects Evil' on, Evil lords and their garrisons shed no Free troops. When off, vanilla. This is the default for new campaigns. With the Alignment rules start option on Standard, a campaign follows this switch live; Strict or Relaxed fixes all four alignment switches for that campaign. Older saves follow this setting.

{=taom_mcm_AlignmentDesertionRate_hint}Fraction of each opposed-alignment troop type that deserts per day (minimum 1 per type). Default 0.50 = half per day. Higher clears mixed parties/garrisons faster.

{=taom_mcm_EnableAlignmentDesertionPlayer_hint}When ON (default), YOUR party and garrisons shed opposed-alignment troops. When OFF, you may keep mixed-alignment troops (AI is still affected if 'Apply To AI Lords' is on).
{=taom_mcm_EnableAlignmentDesertionAi_hint}When ON (default), AI lords' parties and garrisons also shed opposed-alignment troops. When OFF, only the player is affected (if 'Apply To Player' is on).

{=taom_mcm_EnableAlignmentDesertionParties_hint}When ON (default), lords' field parties (including army members) shed opposed troops. When OFF, only garrisons are affected (if 'Apply To Garrisons' is on).

{=taom_mcm_EnableAlignmentDesertionGarrisons_hint}When ON (default), settlement garrisons shed opposed troops (e.g. a conquered fief's old-culture defenders leave). When OFF, only mobile parties are affected (if 'Apply To Mobile Parties' is on).

{=taom_mcm_EnableLordRetinue_hint}When enabled, an AI lord party whose clan is at its party limit takes one idle adult clan member along and gives that member a party role (scout, surgeon, engineer or quartermaster) the member is better at than the lord. The heroes go back to a settlement when the clan drops below its party limit or when this is turned off. When off, no new heroes join. A party whose disband starts always frees every hero aboard but its leader, with this on or off.

{=taom_mcm_LordRetinueMaxExtraHeroes_hint}How many extra clan heroes one AI lord party may carry. Default 1. Heroes already riding along stay when you lower this. A hero who rides along costs the clan a daily wage and a party slot, and can be wounded, captured or killed in battle with the lord.

{=taom_mcm_EnableCombatMechanics_hint}Master toggle for the combat feel pack: skill-based crush-through, monster/orc crush-through, creature cleave, creature stagger immunity, weight-based charge knockdown, shield penetration, race combat modifiers. When off, everything below is inert and combat behaves exactly as before this feature.

{=taom_mcm_EnableSkillCrushThrough_hint}High-energy swings from an attacker who greatly outskills the defender have a chance to crush through the block (chance grows with skill gap and swing momentum; off-angle swings are penalized). Tuning constants live in combat_mechanics_config.json.
{=taom_mcm_EnableMonsterCrushThrough_hint}Troll, mumakil, war elephant and giant spider melee attacks can only be blocked with a SHIELD — a bare-weapon block is crushed through automatically.

{=taom_mcm_EnableOrcShieldCrush_hint}AI orc/uruk swings can crush through even SHIELD blocks (energy- and skill-gated) — turtling against an orc horde is no longer safe. Never applies to the player's own attacks.

{=taom_mcm_EnableCreatureCleave_hint}Troll and mumakil swings slice through a victim and carry 30% momentum into the next — one swing can hit multiple soldiers, including through shield blocks that take damage (a zero-damage block still stops the swing).
{=taom_mcm_EnableCreatureUnstoppable_hint}Big creatures shrug off hits below a per-creature damage threshold — no flinch-locking a troll with arrows. Thresholds live in combat_mechanics_config.json.

{=taom_mcm_EnableChargeKnockdown_hint}Mount charges knock down based on relative weight (charger + rider vs victim), charge speed and the victim's race resistance: a mumakil bowls over infantry, a horse can't floor a troll, dwarves stand their ground.

{=taom_mcm_EnableShieldPenetration_hint}Missiles from config-listed weapon classes/items can penetrate shields and damage the soldier behind. Off by default, and the shipped lists are empty, so javelins behave as in the base game: only a HERO with the Throwing Impale perk pierces a shield. Regular troops never do, in vanilla or here. Turning this on with an empty config changes nothing; add entries in combat_mechanics_config.json first.

{=taom_mcm_EnableRaceCombatModifiers_hint}Per-race combat flavor from combat_mechanics_config.json: dwarves resist knockdown and stagger, elves crush through better and strike true from any angle, orcs swing with brute momentum. When off, all races use neutral values.
{=taom_mcm_CrushThroughMaxChance_hint}Ceiling for the skill-based crush-through chance, reached at a huge skill gap with a full-momentum swing. Default 50%.

{=taom_mcm_ChargeAutoKnockdownRatio_hint}Charger-to-victim weight ratio at which a charge ALWAYS knocks the victim down, from any angle, regardless of resistance (mumakil vs man is ~125, warg + orc vs man 8, horse + man vs man exactly 6). Default 6 since 2026-09-17, so a full-speed horse contact floors a man; raise it to 7 or 8 to give that back to wargs and chariots only. Values below the neutral weight ratio are treated as the neutral ratio. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

{=taom_mcm_ChargeNeutralWeightRatio_hint}Charger-to-victim weight ratio at which a charge knocks down exactly as vanilla does (needs about 8 damage on a head-on hit). Heavier chargers than this ratio get MORE penetration, lighter ones less, down to the min factor. Default 6 = horse + man vs man. Lower it and every charge hits harder; raise it and only the heavy mounts do.

{=taom_mcm_ChargeHorsePenetration_hint}The base knockdown penetration of a charge at the neutral ratio and full speed. Default 0.4, vanilla's value, which cancels a troop's 0.4 base resistance so only Athletics protects him. 0.5 and up floors an ordinary man on any head-on hit that does damage; 0.3 needs a hard hit.

{=taom_mcm_ChargeMinPenetrationFactor_hint}How far below vanilla the weight term may push a light charger's penetration against a heavy victim. Default 1.0 = never below vanilla (uruks and trolls fall like men; the troll, dwarf and Sauron race rows do the resisting). 0.25 restores the pre-2026-09-17 feel where a horse could not floor anything heavier than a man. The ceiling is the JSON's maxPenetrationFactor (shipped 2.5); a slider value above it is treated as that maximum.

{=taom_mcm_EnableCultureChargeDamage_hint}Cavalry charge damage scales by the rider's culture (elves 1.6x, Rohan 1.5x, Rhun 1.4x, Gondor 1.3x, Dale and the orc kingdoms 1.2x, Erebor 1.0x). The table lives in combat_mechanics_config.json; this switch turns the whole thing off.

{=taom_mcm_EnableSignatureStrikes_hint}Configured heroes (shipped: Sauron and the Nine) get direction-mapped effects on any melee hit. Sauron: an overhead is a Slam (the struck foe always goes down, enemies in a ring around the impact are knocked down and take part of the damage, a burst of fear drains their morale; also fires on an overhead into the ground), a side swing is a Sweep (the struck foe and enemies in front are staggered back). The Nine: an overhead or a side swing is a Scream (enemies around the wraith take part of the damage, are staggered back and lose morale; the struck foe is staggered and frightened too). Never on a throw, a shot, a kick or bare hands. The same rules apply in a Custom Battle. Cooldowns and radii live in signature_strikes_config.json.

{=taom_mcm_SignatureStrikeCooldownMultiplier_hint}Multiplies every signature-strike cooldown (shipped: Sauron's Slam 20 s and Sweep 12 s, the Nine's Scream 15 s). Raise it if Sauron or the Nazgul feel overpowered; the JSON values need a full restart, this slider applies live.

{=taom_mcm_EnableShieldBashKnockdown_hint}A shield bash or a kick can floor a man. The chance grows with the attacker's Athletics lead over the victim; the victim's race and any race ability that toughens him cut it, a kick is weaker than a bash, and you resist more than a soldier does. Fighters who shrug off blows never fall: trolls while Creature Stagger Immunity is on, a soldier with a live race ability that shrugs off blows, and a hero with a career shrug-off passive. The numbers live in combat_mechanics_config.json.

{=taom_mcm_EnableDreadAura_hint}Nazgul and Sauron drain the morale of enemy troops right beside them. The aura weakens them so they break sooner in the fighting, but it never routs anyone by itself. Takes effect immediately, but morale already drained is not restored when you switch it off.

{=taom_mcm_DreadAuraCloseRadius_hint}Metres over which a wraith projects dread. Full strength within the inner radius from dread_aura_config.json (default 2m), falling to nothing at this distance. Default 5. The ceiling is 15: beyond 15 m the engine's proximity search stops using its grid and checks every agent on the field, on every pulse.

{=taom_mcm_DreadAuraMoralePerSecond_hint}Morale per second drained at full strength, before the target's tier/hero resistance and its racial resistance. The aura stops at a morale floor of 10 (dread_aura_config.json), so it never routs anyone by itself. At the default 5.0, in an even fight, a tier-3 human reaches the floor after about 22 seconds of contact, a tier-6 elite about 37, and an elven hero of level 16 or more never. Below about 1.0 the engine's own morale recovery outpaces the drain.

{=taom_mcm_DreadAuraAffectsPlayerTroops_hint}When off, your team is immune and dread only touches the AI. Left on, an enemy wraith weakens your soldiers so they rout sooner in combat, and routed troops are LOST from your party. Your own character is always immune either way: the engine gives player-controlled agents no morale component at all.

{=taom_mcm_EnableRaceAbilities_hint}AI soldiers fight with a battle ability for their race (or, for men, their culture) on a cooldown, fired when the moment comes and joined by nearby kin: berserkers go berserk when hurt in melee, Uruk-hai fall into bloodlust on a kill, dwarves stand fast against a charge or a crowd, elves quicken, orcs swarm, Rohan's riders spur on, Gondor closes ranks, and more. Your own character never fires one. Switching it on takes effect from the next battle; switching it off stops new abilities at once and lets running ones finish. Numbers live in race_abilities.json; the console command taom.print_race_abilities shows what each ability has done in the battle on screen.
{=taom_mcm_RaceAbilityWarCries_hint}The soldier who fires an ability, and a few of the kin who join him, shout in their own voice.
{=taom_mcm_RaceAbilityMessages_hint}One line in the message log when five or more soldiers on either side fire the same ability within two seconds. Never one line per soldier.

{=taom_mcm_RaceAbilityDebugLog_hint}Writes one log line for every wave of abilities and every phase change (active, spent, ready). Off, the log still gets a summary every 30 s of activity and at the end of each battle. For checking that the abilities work; leave off in normal play.

{=taom_mcm_RaceAbilityGlow_hint}A soldier whose ability is active wears a coloured outline: red for fury, steel blue for a guard, violet for dread; the speed and aim abilities stay unlit. Sparks burst on the soldier who fires and on a few of the kin who join him. Only the soldiers nearest the camera are outlined (visuals.maxGlowing in race_abilities.json). Drawn on this client only, and hidden while Hide Battle UI is on.
{=taom_mcm_EnableUncapturableHeroes}Sauron and the Nazgûl Cannot Be Captured

{=taom_mcm_EnableUncapturableHeroes_hint}When you beat them, they escape the field as fugitives instead of going to your dungeon, and return with a new army within days. This does NOT make them immortal: one of the Nine can still die in a battle he could not be captured in. Edit uncapturable_heroes_config.json to change who this covers.
{=taom_mcm_EnableNameplateFade_hint}Fade settlement nameplates with camera distance. When off, all nameplates display at full visibility regardless of distance (vanilla).
{=taom_mcm_NameplateFadeNearDistance_hint}Camera distance at which fade begins. Nameplates closer than this stay fully opaque. Default 80.
{=taom_mcm_NameplateFadeFarDistance_hint}Camera distance at which fade completes. Nameplates farther than this are fully hidden. Must be greater than Fade Start Distance. Default 200.

{=taom_mcm_EnableNameplateRelationColors_hint}Tint each settlement plate by your relation to its owner: green for your own faction, red for an enemy, blue for an allied kingdom, plain parchment for neutral. Off leaves every plate parchment. Applies immediately.

{=taom_mcm_NameplateRelationTintStrength_hint}How strongly the relation colour is applied to the bar, the name and the diamond frame. 100 is the full palette, 0 is plain parchment for everyone. Applies immediately. Default 100.

{=taom_mcm_NameplateNeutralPlateOpacity_hint}Opacity of a neutral settlement's plate. Vanilla uses 35, which can be faint over dark terrain. Tracked settlements keep vanilla's 80. Applies immediately. Default 35.

{=taom_mcm_NameplateRelationPlateOpacity_hint}Opacity of a plate owned by your own faction, an enemy or an allied kingdom. Vanilla uses 50 for your own faction and 35 for the others. Tracked settlements keep vanilla's 80. Applies immediately. Default 50.

{=taom_mcm_MapFigureScale_hint}Size of party-icon figures and their mounts on the campaign map. Vanilla = 0.30; default 0.15 = half (makes parties feel smaller relative to settlements). Applies on the next icon rebuild after changing.

{=taom_mcm_HiddenHostsEnabled_hint}Another party's troop count on the campaign map blurs with its distance from you: '1??', '12?', then exact as you close in, and '...' at the very edge of sight. Standing closer, a higher Scouting skill and hosts of your own realm all sharpen it. Wounded and prisoner counts show only when the count is exact. A count you read stays remembered with a '~' and fades by the hour, and reading an enemy host's count from afar trains your scout's Scouting; Off stops both. AI lords still see true numbers. A host's orders in its hover tooltip stay hidden until its count is exact. Off = vanilla counts and orders. Applies immediately. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_ForestSightPenaltyEnabled_hint}In vanilla, forest makes other parties harder for you to see and slows your party by 20%; it never hides your party from anyone. With this on, your own sight on the campaign map also shrinks by 30% of your base sight while your party travels through forest, and by half that if your scout has the Keen Sight perk. It does not apply inside a settlement. A raised lookout, perks and a Far Watch ride still add to your sight, and the penalties together never take more than half of your base sight. Only your own party is affected; AI parties see as before. The map bar view distance shows the shorter range, but its tooltip has no line for the forest. Off = vanilla sight in forest. Applies immediately. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableFiefGrantRebalance_hint}Rebalances who gets a captured town or castle. Off = exact vanilla, where the ruling clan's +60 merit and its unlimited King's Vote override let it take fief after fief. Does not change starting ownership. The ballot's fief count shows either way.

{=taom_mcm_FiefGrantCapturerBonus_hint}Merit multiplier for the clan that carried the winning assault: the largest share of the winning besieging side's battle contribution, the same number the loot split uses. Every other clan of that kingdom that fielded a party there gets it in proportion, 1 + (bonus - 1) x its share of the top clan's contribution, so a clan with half the top clan's contribution gets half the bonus. Mercenaries and allies from other kingdoms cannot be granted the fief and are not counted. Vanilla's flat +30 for the assault leader's clan is untouched. 1.00 = off. Default: 2.50.

{=taom_mcm_FiefGrantAbsentFromSiegeFactor_hint}Merit multiplier for a clan that had no party in the winning assault, so land goes to the houses that fought for it. Applies to your clan as well, exempt or not: this is about what a clan did, not what it holds. No effect when nothing is on record for the settlement, such as a fief that changed hands without an assault. 1.00 = off. Default: 0.50.

{=taom_mcm_FiefGrantLandlessBonus_hint}Merit multiplier for a clan that holds no town or castle at all. Keeps poor clans able to field parties instead of withering and leaving the kingdom. Vanilla already favours landless clans (a flat +30 and nothing in its holdings divisor), so this stacks on a strong base. 1.00 = no bonus. Default: 2.00.

{=taom_mcm_FiefGrantConcentrationPenalty_hint}How hard each fief a clan already holds counts against its next claim, as 1/(1 + fiefs x penalty). Vanilla only divides by the VALUE it holds, so a clan sitting on many cheap castles is barely damped. 0.00 = off. Default: 0.35.

{=taom_mcm_FiefGrantCultureMatchBonus_hint}Merit multiplier when the clan's culture matches the settlement's. Vanilla has no equivalent, which is how an orc clan ends up holding an elven city. 1.00 = off. Default: 1.50.
{=taom_mcm_FiefGrantCultureMismatchPenalty_hint}Merit multiplier when it does not match. Lower means foreign clans rarely win a settlement of another culture. 1.00 = off. Default: 0.60.

{=taom_mcm_FiefGrantRulingClanFactor_hint}Merit multiplier for the king's own clan, which vanilla already hands a flat +60 on top of its tier and strength. Below 1.00 damps the crown's claim. 1.00 = vanilla. Default: 0.75.

{=taom_mcm_FiefGrantKingsVoteFiefShareCap_hint}Share of the kingdom's towns and castles above which the ruling clan loses its right to overrule the council. Vanilla lets a king with enough influence override every grant, and his pick is always himself. 1.00 = vanilla. Default: 0.34.

{=taom_mcm_FiefGrantExemptPlayerClanFromPenalties_hint}On = your clan keeps every bonus but is never damped for the fiefs it already holds or for a culture mismatch. Off = your clan is scored like any other. Replaces the old Apply Penalties To Your Clan switch, which shipped with the exemption on and let a landed player out-score every AI clan for fiefs they never fought for; the switch was renamed so existing installs pick up the new default. The Absent From Siege Factor applies either way. Default: off.

{=taom_mcm_EnableDwarfEyeHeight_hint}Lower a dwarf eye height so the third-person camera sits at the head instead of floating above it. Applies to every dwarf, not just the player, so it also moves the aim origin for dwarf troops. Changing this takes effect the next time a dwarf visual is built (opening a character preview, or the next dwarf spawn), not the instant you flip it.

{=taom_mcm_DwarfEyeHeightAdjuster_hint}Metres relative to the human eye height. Negative lowers the camera. Default -0.20. The resulting height is clamped to a safe range, so extreme values cannot put the camera in the floor. Like the toggle above, a change lands the next time a dwarf visual is built.

{=taom_mcm_EnableSupplyLines_hint}Order resupply convoys from a town, castle or friendly lord: goods from real market stock, troops from volunteers, delivered to you on the map. When off, the order option disappears and no new orders can be placed; convoys already on the road still arrive.
{=taom_mcm_SupplyGoodsMarkupFactor_hint}Price multiplier on ordered goods over their market value. Default 1.05.
{=taom_mcm_SupplyTransportFeePerDistance_hint}Delivery fee per map-distance unit between the source and your party. Default 2.
{=taom_mcm_SupplyMercenaryWagePerDistance_hint}Cost of a mercenary escort per map-distance unit. Default 10.
{=taom_mcm_SupplyMercenaryGuardCount_hint}Guards added to the convoy when a mercenary escort is hired. Default 10.
{=taom_mcm_SupplyCaravanHoursPerDistance_hint}Convoy travel time per map-distance unit. Default 2. Lower is faster delivery.
{=taom_mcm_SupplyShowRouteVisual_hint}Draw the arrow trail from the source to your party while a convoy is on the road. Presentation only.

{=taom_mcm_EnableFieldCamps_hint}Pitch camps on the campaign map: field and fortified camps with morale and foraging, terrain-gated ambushes and lookouts. When off, the Make Camp button and camp menus disappear; an existing camp stays until you break it.
{=taom_mcm_CampSetupHours_hint}Hours to raise a field camp. Ambushes and lookouts take a quarter of this; a fortified camp double. Default 4.
{=taom_mcm_CampMoralePerHour_hint}Party morale gained per camped hour once the camp is raised; fortified camps double it. Default 1.
{=taom_mcm_CampForagePerTroopFactor_hint}Foraging throughput per troop. Grain per hour also scales with terrain, the party's Scouting skill and the square root of troop count. Default 0.10.
{=taom_mcm_CampMaxAmbushRange_hint}Spotting distance inside which an armed ambush can spring on a passing hostile party. Default 10.
{=taom_mcm_CampBaseAmbushChance_hint}Base chance an eligible passer-by springs the ambush; proximity and Scouting raise it. Default 0.50.
{=taom_mcm_CampMinTownDistance_hint}Keep-out radius from towns and castles for pitching a field or fortified camp. 0 disables the check; ambushes and lookouts are exempt. Default 10.
{=taom_mcm_CampFortifiedUpgradeCost_hint}Gold to fortify a raised field camp. Default 500.
{=taom_mcm_CampActivityHours_hint}Hours a camp work (hunt, fell timber, fish) takes once the men are set to it. Default 10.
{=taom_mcm_CampActivityYieldPerTenMen_hint}Goods a finished camp work brings in for every ten healthy men, on the best ground for it; poorer ground brings in less. Default 10.
{=taom_mcm_CampActivityYieldCap_hint}Most goods one finished camp work can bring in, however many men are sent. Default 30.

{=taom_mcm_CampRestHealRegularsPerDay_hint}Extra wounded troops healed per day: a base amount that the usual healing percentages raise too. Works only while the camp panel is open (Camp Options, then Manage camp); the work menus do not count (set both to 0 to turn rest healing off, lodging perks included). Default 15.

{=taom_mcm_CampRestHealHeroesPerDay_hint}Extra hit points per day for wounded heroes: a base amount that the usual healing percentages raise too. Works only while the camp panel is open (Camp Options, then Manage camp); the work menus do not count (set both to 0 to turn rest healing off, lodging perks included). Default 19.

{=taom_mcm_CampStartInCamp_hint}A new campaign begins with a field camp pitched where the party starts, if the ground allows it; otherwise a message says why and the game goes on as usual. Off by default.

{=taom_mcm_EnableRefuges_hint}Raise a field or fortified camp into a persistent, garrisonable base. When off: no founding, no upgrading, and your party is not held in place during a build. Standing refuges persist, builds in progress still finish, and refuges can still be entered, managed and dismantled.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeStrongholdUpgradeCost_hint}Gold to upgrade a refuge into a stronghold. Default 5000.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeBuildHours_hint}Hours to raise a refuge after founding; the stronghold rebuild takes the same. Default 6.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeMaxCap_hint}Ceiling on simultaneous refuges. The live limit is min(1 + clan tier / 2, this cap). Default 3.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeManageRange_hint}How close your party must be to manage a refuge's garrison and stores. Default 4.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeMinTownDistance_hint}Founding keep-out radius from towns and castles. Default 16.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeStrongholdMinTownDistance_hint}Stronghold-upgrade keep-out radius from towns and castles. Default 26.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeDefenseBonus_hint}Damage reduction for troops defending a refuge, in battle and in auto-resolve. Default 0.20.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeStrongholdDefenseBonus_hint}Damage reduction for troops defending a stronghold. Default 0.35.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeMilitiaBase_hint}Base temporary militia rallying to a refuge under attack; age of the refuge and garrison size add more. Default 6.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeMilitiaMax_hint}Ceiling on the temporary defence militia. Default 40.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeEnableRaids_hint}Experimental: hostile parties can attack your refuges (auto-resolved when you are away). Off by default.
{=taom_mcm_RefugeRaidRange_hint}Search radius around a refuge for raid candidates when raids are enabled. Default 6.

{=taom_mcm_EnablePlayerSwitcher_hint}Adds a panel to the character creation face generator listing the existing lords of your chosen culture. Pick one and you play the campaign as that lord, with their face, gear, skills, clan, fiefs and kingdom. The character you build is set aside. Off means the panel never loads and character creation is untouched. When the Themed Faction & Hero Picker (Menus & Loading Screens) is shown, it takes this panel's place for that character creation, and a lord picked there is taken over through this feature, so with this off that picker copies the lord's look, gear and skills onto your own character instead.

{=taom_mcm_PlayerSwitcherIncludeWanderers_hint}Also lists the wanderers of your culture. A wanderer has no clan, so instead of taking over a house they are adopted into the clan you named, with the banner you designed, and you lead it. Only 20 of 39 cultures have any wanderers.

{=taom_mcm_PlayerSwitcherAllowDarkLords_hint}Offers the lore-locked dark lords as playable, here and on the Themed Faction & Hero Picker. On by default. The catch: TAOM's capture immunity defers to vanilla for the player character, so a player-controlled Sauron or Witch-king CAN be captured and ransomed like any other lord. Turn this off to keep that lore promise: this list then hides them, and a pick of one on the Themed Faction & Hero Picker only copies his look onto a new character. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

{=taom_mcm_PlayerSwitcherTransferStartingGold_hint}When you take over a lord, adds the starting gold your created character was given on top of the lord's own treasury. An adopted wanderer starts with a new character's gold either way, and an Advanced Start type other than the default sets its own gold. Off by default: an established lord is already funded, so stacking a startup package on them is a balance change rather than a fix.
{=taom_mcm_FrontEndCustomMainMenu_hint}Kysaro's Middle-earth main menu in place of the vanilla one. Takes effect the next time the main menu opens.

{=taom_mcm_FrontEndHideGameVersion_hint}Hides the Bannerlord version number in the corner of the main menu. The TAOM log still records it. Takes effect after a restart: the game builds the version line once, at startup.
{=taom_mcm_FrontEndMenuVideo_hint}Plays the Sauron video behind the main menu in place of the vanilla background video. Takes effect the next time the main menu opens.

{=taom_mcm_FrontEndMuteMenuMusic_hint}Keeps the vanilla menu theme off the main menu while the menu video plays its own soundtrack, so it needs Main Menu Video on. Vanilla's music returns once you leave the main menu. Takes effect the next time the main menu opens.

{=taom_mcm_FrontEndCustomLoadingImages_hint}Shows Kysaro's Middle-earth paintings on loading screens, never the same one twice in a row. Only the picture last shown is kept in memory. Takes effect on the next loading screen.

{=taom_mcm_FrontEndSkillIcons_hint}Kysaro's skill icons in place of the vanilla ones, everywhere in the game. Turning them on applies the next time the main menu opens; turning them off takes effect after a restart, because the vanilla icons are not kept once replaced.

{=taom_mcm_FrontEndFactionScreen_hint}Kysaro's faction screen with painted portraits, a map and a hero picker, in place of TAOM's faction map. Picking one of that faction's lords or ladies makes you that character, with their clan, fiefs and kingdom: character creation goes straight to the career choice and then into the game (Player Switcher's settings apply). Picking a legend or any other character starts you with its look, gear and skills. When it is shown it takes the place of Player Switcher's panel for that character creation. Takes effect the next time character creation reaches the culture screen.
{=taom_mcm_FrontEndCustomFaceGen_hint}Kysaro's reskin of the character creation face generator. Outside character creation the face generator stays vanilla. Takes effect the next time it opens.
{=taom_mcm_FrontEndCustomNarrativeStage_hint}Kysaro's reskin of the family, childhood, adolescence, youth, adulthood and age screens. Takes effect the next time one of them opens.
{=taom_mcm_FrontEndCustomReviewStage_hint}Kysaro's reskin of the final review screen, where you name your character. Takes effect the next time it opens.
{=taom_mcm_FrontEndCustomBannerEditor_hint}The themed, layered banner editor, both during character creation and in a running campaign. Takes effect the next time it opens.
{=taom_mcm_FrontEndCustomClanNaming_hint}Kysaro's reskin of the clan naming screen. Takes effect the next time it opens.
{=taom_mcm_FrontEndCustomOptionsStage_hint}Kysaro's reskin of the difficulty and campaign options screen at the end of character creation. Takes effect the next time it opens.

{=taom_mcm_RebuildDistanceCacheAction_hint}Spawns a 10-30 minute background task that recomputes the settlement distance cache against the live map scene. Requires an active campaign. Game stays playable but pathfinding queries during the rebuild may be inconsistent — best run from main menu after loading a save.

{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditSpawnBroods_hint}Whether spider broods keep spawning around Mirkwood and Dol Guldur on the campaign map (one a day, up to twenty). Off stops new broods; broods already on the map stay. Broods exist only in a campaign started with v2.0.32 or later.

{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditSpawnTrollBands_hint}Whether wild troll bands keep spawning on the campaign map, about one per kingdom near its towns, castles and villages (one new band a day, two to four trolls each). Trolls are never taken prisoner or recruited. Off stops new bands; bands already on the map stay. Troll bands need a new campaign. The options below tune the spiders only.

{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditHitPoints_hint}Hit points of a riderless creature bandit (the giant spiders of the Mirkwood broods). The ridden spider mount keeps its own. Applies to creatures spawned after the change.
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditBiteTargets_hint}How many soldiers the standing front bite can strike at once (the nearest ones in its arc).
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditPounceTargets_hint}How many soldiers the running pounce can strike at once.
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditSwipeTargets_hint}How many soldiers a left or right swipe can strike at once.
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditBiteDamagePercent_hint}Bite damage as a percentage of the spider's base bite (100 = the ridden spider's damage).
