{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditPounceDamagePercent_hint}Pounce damage as a percentage of the spider's base bite.
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditSwipeDamagePercent_hint}Swipe damage as a percentage of the spider's base bite. Low by default: the swipe reaches several soldiers.

{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditKnockdownOnCritOnly_hint}When on, a creature's normal hit only staggers a soldier and only a critical hit knocks him down. When off, any hit of 30 or more knocks down, as the ridden spider's do.
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditPounceCooldownSeconds_hint}Seconds between a creature's pounces or bites. Applies to creatures spawned after the change.
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditSwipeCooldownSeconds_hint}Seconds between a creature's swipes. Applies to creatures spawned after the change.
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditMissileTakenPercent_hint}Share of damage a creature takes from arrows, bolts, javelins and thrown weapons (100 = normal). Applies at once.
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditCutTakenPercent_hint}Share of damage a creature takes from cutting melee blows: swords, axes (100 = normal).
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditPierceTakenPercent_hint}Share of damage a creature takes from piercing melee blows: spears, thrusts (100 = normal).
{=taom_mcm_CreatureBanditBluntTakenPercent_hint}Share of damage a creature takes from blunt melee blows: maces, hammers, charges (100 = normal).

{=taom_mcm_EnableRealmBorders_hint}Draws each kingdom's border on the campaign map, following rivers, coasts and mountain ranges, and redraws it when a fief changes hands. While this is on, the Show Realm Borders key (M by default) hides and shows them, and the map mode key (G) switches what they show.
{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersHeraldicBands_hint}Off: the Atlas look, a watercolour wash inside each border with a dash-dot ink line. On: two solid bands in each realm's colour with a gap on the line.
{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersGildPlayerRealm_hint}Draws your own kingdom's frontier as a gold cord, so you can find it at a glance.
{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersWidthScale_hint}Multiplies the width of every border. Default: 1.

{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersFadeStartDistance_hint}Camera distance at which the borders start to appear; closer than this they are hidden. Must be below Full Opacity Distance, or both revert to their defaults. Default: 45.
{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersFullOpacityDistance_hint}Camera distance at which the borders are fully drawn. Default: 110.
{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersDrawThroughTerrain_hint}On: borders always show, drawn over hills and map figures. Off: borders lie on the ground and hide behind ridges.
{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersNames_hint}Letters each kingdom's name across its land when the camera is zoomed out.
{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersCrossingNotices_hint}Tells you when your party rides into another kingdom's lands.
{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersFillLands_hint}Tints each kingdom's land in its colour between the borders, like a map in an atlas.
{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersFillStrength_hint}How strongly the land is tinted: 0.05 is a faint wash, 0.8 nearly paints over the map. Default: 0.5.

{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersParchmentMap_hint}As you zoom all the way out, a parchment map of Middle-earth fades in over the campaign map, with the borders, realm colours and names drawn on it. It shows only while the borders do.

{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersBlendMode_hint}Advanced: how the borders mix with the map beneath. 'Material default' keeps the engine material's own. If the borders glow and their dark ink line is missing, try Modulate (Factor turns blending off).

{=taom_mcm_RealmBordersMaterial_hint}Advanced: the engine material the borders are drawn from. 'Automatic' tries vertex_color_blend_after_postfx_mat first, which blends normally so the dark ink line shows, then the others in list order. Every choice draws over the parchment map.

{=taom_mcm_EnableRandomStepSize_hint}Orc and goblin warriors in a battle line no longer walk in lockstep: each soldier's step size is scaled by a random factor between the minimum below and 1.0, fixed for that soldier. Applied when a soldier spawns, so it takes effect in the next battle.

{=taom_mcm_GaitStepSizeMinFactor_hint}Each soldier's step size is vanilla's step size times a random factor between this value and 1.00. Vanilla's own step size is 0.80 at Athletics 0 and rises to 1.00 at Athletics 300, so the factor is not the final step size: at 0.92 an Athletics 0 soldier ends at 0.74 to 0.80 and an Athletics 300 soldier at 0.92 to 1.00, and at 0.80 the lowest step size is 0.64. 1.00 turns the spread off. A value outside 0.80 to 1.00 falls back to 0.92.

{=taom_mcm_EnableRandomGaitSet_hint}Each orc and goblin warrior walks with one of several gait sets, picked at random and fixed for that soldier. A gait set that is not installed is skipped, so with none installed this does nothing. Applied when a soldier spawns, so it takes effect in the next battle.

{=taom_mcm_EnableSwingAlternativeProbe_hint}Tests alternative swing clips: when a mission has act_taom_ swing codes loaded, it counts which clip each swing plays and where in the clip a hit lands, and only logs; it changes nothing in the game. While such codes exist it costs a per-frame sweep of every person in every mission, towns included; with none loaded it writes one log line per mission. Read at the start of each mission.

{=taom_mcm_EnableWatchfulHolds_hint}When enabled (default), a castle or town whose realm is at war with yours harasses a lord party that marches within a few map units of its walls, if the fort is not besieged and holds enough troops (30 by default). Your party is slowed (disorganized: it moves slower, and its troops start a battle with lower morale until it wears off) and loses a few men, some food and morale. An army you lead loses cohesion, but never below 10, and each party marching with you takes its own losses. When off, forts never harass anyone. Applies at once, no restart.

{=taom_mcm_WatchfulHoldsHarassAiLords_hint}When enabled (default), AI lords marching past an enemy fort are slowed (disorganized) too, at a lower chance than yours, and lose nothing else. Turn it off to protect the campaign pace: the effect then stays on your own party and the army you lead (AI lords marching with your army still take their share). Does nothing while Enable Watchful Holds is off.

{=taom_mcm_EnableFireAndTribute_hint}When enabled (default), raiding hosts ride once the War of the Ring is in Full War, or from day 89 when the War of the Ring is switched off. They ride out of their homelands to burn the villages of the opposed side: Orcs of Gundabad, Easterlings of Rhûn, Haradrim, Dunlendings and the Blacklocks of Erebor against the Free Peoples; outlaw bands of Gondor and Mirkwood against the Shadow; Corsairs of Umbar against either. A host raids the villages of the strongest enemy realm, fights weaker parties of that realm it meets, and goes home after its quota. When off, no host rides and a host already out is sent away at its next hourly tick; one still fighting is sent away once its battle ends. Single player only. Applies at once, no restart.
{=taom_mcm_FireAndTributeFreeHosts_hint}When enabled (default), the outlaw bands of Gondor and Mirkwood may ride against the Shadow's realms. Does nothing while Enable Fire and Tribute is off.
{=taom_mcm_FireAndTributeNeutralHosts_hint}When enabled (default), the Corsair Host of Umbar may ride against Free or Shadow realms. Does nothing while Enable Fire and Tribute is off.

{=taom_mcm_FireAndTributeEvilHosts_hint}When enabled (default), the hosts of Gundabad, Rhûn, Harad and Dunland, and the Blacklocks of Erebor, may ride against the Free Peoples' realms. Does nothing while Enable Fire and Tribute is off.

{=taom_mcm_FireAndTributeEnvoys_hint}When enabled (default), a host that rides against your kingdom sends an envoy a day or two later, if your clan owns villages and you are not enlisted. The envoy asks for gold, at a price that grows with your villages and with each envoy you have seized. Pay and the host raids none of your clan's villages and never attacks your party; haggle once (a Charm roll) when the tribute is large; ask for time; refuse; or seize the envoy, after which that side's next host rides against your kingdom first. Shown only while the map is free. When off, no envoy is scheduled or shown. Single player only. Applies at once, no restart.

{=taom_mcm_EnableUnlookedForAid_hint}When enabled (default), an AI lord stops running from an army that besieges a settlement when the lord, with its army if it leads one or is attached to it, is at least half as strong as the entire siege camp (0.5 by default, unlooked_for_aid.json). Lords can then pass a siege or gather near it. A lord shut inside a besieged settlement is never fled from, whatever the strengths. A weaker lord still flees, so it is not caught when the siege lifts beside it. At a siege you lead, AI lords keep the base game behaviour. Caravans, villagers, bandits, patrols and garrisons are unchanged. When off, lords flee exactly as in the base game. Applies at once, no restart.

{=taom_mcm_EnableRedArrow_hint}When enabled (default), the Army Management screen works during a siege you lead as the besieger: you can call parties into your army and release them while the siege goes on, at the usual influence cost. The base game's other limits still apply (a party that is fighting, too weak, disbanding, too far away or at sea is refused, and so is a party already at the siege outside your army). Defending a siege, having no army and being in a map event keep the base game block. Singleplayer only: in a co-op session this does nothing. When off, the block is exactly the base game's. Takes effect the next time the screen opens, no restart.

{=taom_mcm_EnableKingsMusterDiscount_hint}When enabled (default), an AI kingdom ruler, Good or Evil, pays half the influence (0.5 by default, RulerCallCostFactor in army_targeting.json) for each party called into an army, after culture feats. Cheaper calls also make the influence an army spends on keeping itself together cheaper for the ruler, so those hosts hold longer and the ruler's clan keeps more influence for votes. Your own calls, as a ruler or a vassal, cost what they always did. Singleplayer only: in a co-op session this does nothing. When off, the ruler pays the usual cost; culture feats and the Realms liege army discount still apply. The two discounts do not stack: when both apply to a call, the larger one is used. Applies at once, no restart.

{=taom_mcm_BondsOfBattleEnabled_hint}Relation with lords and notables is earned on campaign: fighting beside a lord, clearing bandits near a settlement, handing a lord troops, and overpaying in a barter. Off restores vanilla on all four. Does nothing while you are enlisted. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_BondsAllyBonus_hint}Relation gained with each lord who fought on your side in a battle, once per lord per battle (once per clan when Personal Relations is off, because a clan then shares one relation). Your own clan, an army you lead and lords leading no party earn nothing; after a win, the side leader you came to help is thanked by vanilla's own conversation instead, but only when vanilla pays him something (a small contribution earns him this bonus). 0 = none. Default: 1.

{=taom_mcm_BondsEnemyPenaltyEnabled_hint}Each lord who fought against you in a battle thinks less of you, once per lord per battle (once per clan when Personal Relations is off, because a clan then shares one relation). Bandits are never counted. Default: off.
{=taom_mcm_BondsEnemyPenalty_hint}How much relation each enemy lord loses when the option above is on. 0 = none. Default: 5.

{=taom_mcm_BondsBanditGratitudeEnabled_hint}In the field, against bandits alone (cleared hideouts are thanked by vanilla): after you win, one random notable in each settlement near the battle gains relation with you, one point for every ten bandits killed, wounded or routed, at least 1 and at most 10. A village in the other side's land (Free against Evil) does not thank you. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_BondsBanditGratitudeRadius_hint}How far from the battle, in map units, a settlement still thanks you. A settlement is usually about 17 units from its nearest neighbour. Default: 25.

{=taom_mcm_BondsTroopHandoverEnabled_hint}When you hand troops to another lord on the Donate Troops screen, that lord gains relation with you: half of the influence the gift is worth, at most 10, give or take one. A gift worth less than 2 earns nothing. Hand-overs stop paying a lord once 10 relation has landed with him that day; the Done that reaches 10 asks only for what is left, and Charm can raise it. A lord gains at most 10 a day from hand-overs, however the gift is split (Charm can raise the last Done). The same rule pays for troops given to a lord through a Lord Courtesies gift. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_BondsOverpayRelationCap_hint}The most relation one barter can buy by offering more than the goods are worth. The loop buys at most 3 points in vanilla (the setting here), before the Tribute perk (x1.2, rounded up) and the Charm relation bonus the engine adds when it applies the change. Points cost more the further relation is from 0, so only a large overpay reaches the cap. Default: 15.

{=taom_mcm_PersonalRelationsEnabled_hint}Your relation with a lord stays with that lord instead of passing to his clan leader, so a friendship with Faramir is not a friendship with Denethor. Affects only your own relations: relations between AI lords stay vanilla. Single player only: in a co-op session or on a dedicated server it stays vanilla. A save made before this was on is seeded once: on the first day this is on, each living lord whose personal relation with you is 0 takes his clan leader's value, and it is seeded again when this has been off for at least one in-game day. Off restores vanilla. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_PersonalDisbandCostEnabled_hint}Paying influence to disband another lord's army costs you relation with the army's leader by the amounts below (vanilla is 4); each other lord in it costs vanilla's 1. Applies only in single player, and only while Enable Personal Relations is on. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_PersonalDisbandLeaderMin_hint}The least relation you lose with an army's leader when you pay influence to disband it. The cost is a random whole number between the least and the most. If the least is above the most, the two swap. Applies only in single player, and only while Enable Personal Relations is on. Default: 28.

{=taom_mcm_PersonalDisbandLeaderMax_hint}The most relation you lose with an army's leader when you pay influence to disband it. Applies only in single player, and only while Enable Personal Relations is on. Default: 32.

{=taom_mcm_FellFoesCorneredRouters_hint}A routing enemy soldier who has just been hit, with a few of your men right beside him and enough health left, turns and fights instead of running on, and routers close to him turn with him (a few at most). They keep fighting only while one of your men is still near them and some of their side still stand; once the whole side has broken they run again, so the battle still ends in a rout. Soldiers of cultures that never rout, and soldiers ordered to retreat, are not touched. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_FellFoesCorneredMaxFoes_hint}A routing soldier turns to fight only while this many of your men or fewer are within a few steps of him. Default: 3.

{=taom_mcm_FellFoesArchersTargetPlayer_hint}Enemy archers that have nothing to shoot at, are steady, and are within bow range of you may fix on you and shoot, for a few seconds at a time. A cap keeps the volley small. Archers of a team that is making a stand against horse are left to that stand. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_FellFoesArcherChance_hint}The chance each second that an idle archer in range fixes on you. 0 never, 1 always. Default: 0.25.
{=taom_mcm_FellFoesArcherMaxHolding_hint}The most enemy archers that hold you as their target at the same moment. Default: 8.

{=taom_mcm_FellFoesStragglersLeave_hint}In a large field battle, when only a few enemy soldiers are left, none of them a hero and none still to arrive, the survivors are sent off the field after a pause so the battle ends in your win and they can be taken prisoner. Sieges and sally-outs are not changed. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_FellFoesStragglerMaxCount_hint}The cleanup starts when this many enemy soldiers or fewer are left. Default: 3.
{=taom_mcm_FellFoesStragglerHoldSeconds_hint}Seconds the battle must stay down to the last few before the survivors are sent off, one a second. Default: 30.

{=taom_mcm_FellFoesDebug_hint}Writes a [FellFoes] line each second something is stopped, held or sent off, and whether held archers really are aiming at you. For checking the feature; leave off in normal play. Default: off.

{=taom_mcm_GiftsEnabled_hint}Adds "I have a gift for you." to the talk with the companions in your party and, on the diplomacy branch, with lords who are not children, not prisoners, not in your own clan and not at war with you. Goods the catalog lists, from your inventory, win relation; companions also take gold purses. A co-op client, or a peer running a co-op mod TAOM cannot probe, sees no gift line. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_GiftCooldownDays_hint}After a gift, the same hero takes no other for this many days, so goods cannot be turned straight into relation. Whenever Personal Relations is not engaged (switched off, a co-op host, or a save not yet seeded) a clan shares one relation, so the days count for the whole clan. The count is saved with the campaign. Default: 7.

{=taom_mcm_GiftRelationCap_hint}The most relation one gift asks for, after the taste bonus and the scaling by relation (above relation 0 a gift adds (90 minus relation) / 90 of its worth, so a 1-point gift stops working near relation 45 and nothing helps at 90). A companion's gift starts at 1 to 5 by the item's value; a lord's starts at the catalog's value for the goods (1 to 10), and a hero who prizes the goods adds a bonus. Your Charm can add to what lands. Default: 15.
{=taom_mcm_GiftAlignmentRefusal}Free Lords Refuse Gifts From Evil Players

{=taom_mcm_GiftAlignmentRefusal_hint}A lord of a Free realm will not take a gift from a player who sides with the Shadow. The lord refuses with no penalty. Realms and cultures that side with neither never refuse. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_GiftPurseSmall_hint}The gold in the smallest purse you can give a companion. The gold leaves you and goes to the companion. A purse is worth 1 relation per 500 gold, at most 10 (5000 gold), before the scaling and the cap. Between 500 and 5000 gold. Default: 500.
{=taom_mcm_GiftPurseMedium_hint}The gold in the middle purse you can give a companion. A purse is worth 1 relation per 500 gold, at most 10 (5000 gold). Between 500 and 5000 gold. Default: 2000.
{=taom_mcm_GiftPurseLarge_hint}The gold in the largest purse you can give a companion. A purse is worth 1 relation per 500 gold, at most 10 (5000 gold). Between 500 and 5000 gold. Default: 5000.

{=taom_mcm_LostFootingCensus_hint}Counts soldiers, mounts and creatures that are stuck in a battle, standing off the walkable ground or wading in water without moving, and writes what it finds to the log with a [LostFooting] tag, with a summary when the battle ends. It only watches: it never moves or changes anything in the battle. With the rescue on, the start line and the summary are still written. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_LostFootingRescue_hint}Moves a soldier who stays stuck back to where he can walk: off the walkable ground or still in water for 10 seconds, he steps to the nearest good spot within 6 m at his own height; still stuck after 30 seconds, he moves to his place in his formation while you are at least 25 m away. A riderless horse gets the short step only. Never the player, fleeing men, creatures, men working a ladder or machine, or men holding a set post or waiting at a ladder. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs, not co-op. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsEnabled_hint}Turns the three rewards on or off together: relation for releasing a captured lord, for donating a hero prisoner to a settlement and for winning a town's tournament. Each reward also has its own switch below. Applies on the host in co-op. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsReleaseEnabled_hint}Releasing a captured lord from your party (in conversation or on the party screen) or from your own dungeon earns relation with the lord, with the lord's living spouse and with the lord's clan leader. The post-battle "free to go" choice, ransom, peace, escape and any AI release earn nothing. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsDonationEnabled_hint}Handing a hero prisoner to a settlement adds a bonus to the relation vanilla gives with the settlement owner's clan leader. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsTournamentEnabled_hint}Winning a town's tournament earns relation with the owner's clan leader (unless your clan owns the town) and with every notable in the town. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsReleaseLordAmount_hint}Relation asked for with the lord you release, before the alignment multiplier. Vanilla pays another 4 in the conversation. Your Charm can add to what lands. Default: 5.
{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsReleaseSpouseAmount_hint}Relation asked for with the lord's living spouse, before the alignment multiplier. Default: 2.
{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsReleaseLeaderAmount}Release: Relation With The Lord's Clan Leader

{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsReleaseLeaderAmount_hint}Relation asked for with the leader of the lord's clan, before the alignment multiplier. While Personal Relations is off, the lord and the clan leader share one relation, so only the larger of the two is paid. Default: 2.

{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsDonationAmount_hint}Relation added to what vanilla gives with the settlement owner's clan leader for each hero prisoner donated, before the alignment multiplier. Vanilla itself pays nothing when the captive likes the owner. Default: 5.

{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsTournamentAmount_hint}Relation asked for with the town owner's clan leader and with each notable in the town when you win its tournament, before the alignment multiplier. Between 0 and 10. Default: 1.

{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsReleaseSame_hint}Multiplier on every release reward when you and the lord are on the same side (both Free, or both Shadow). Results round half away from zero, and 0 grants nothing. Default: 1.00.
{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsReleaseNeutral_hint}Multiplier on every release reward when you or the lord is on neither side. Default: 0.75.
{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsReleaseOpposite_hint}Multiplier on every release reward when you and the lord are on opposite sides, so freeing an enemy of your cause earns little. Default: 0.50.

{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsDonationSame_hint}Multiplier on the donation relation when the captive and the settlement owner are on the same side. Zero means no reward, and no vanilla relation either, for jailing a friend of the owner. Default: 0.00.
{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsDonationNeutral_hint}Multiplier on the donation relation when the captive or the settlement owner is on neither side. Default: 1.00.

{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsDonationOpposite_hint}Multiplier on the donation relation (vanilla's gain plus the bonus) when the captive is on the opposite side to the settlement owner, such as a Mordor captive handed to Minas Tirith. Default: 2.00.
{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsTournamentSame_hint}Multiplier on the tournament relation with an owner or notable on your side. Default: 1.00.
{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsTournamentNeutral_hint}Multiplier on the tournament relation with an owner or notable who, or whose realm, is on neither side. Default: 1.00.
{=taom_mcm_GoodDeedsTournamentOpposite_hint}Multiplier on the tournament relation with an owner or notable on the opposite side, who does not cheer a champion of the other cause. Default: 0.00.

{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryEnabled_hint}Turns on the extra relation loss, on top of vanilla's own, that a village's owner and notables hold against you when you raid the village or force it to give goods or recruits. Villages your clan owns are never affected, and neither are raids you do not lead. Applies on the host in co-op. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryRaidEnabled_hint}A raid you lead costs relation with the owner's clan leader and with every notable of the village, in proportion to the damage the raid did. A raid that did none costs nothing. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryCoercionEnabled_hint}Forcing a village to give goods or recruits costs relation with the owner's clan leader and with every notable, whether the villagers resist or give way. A resisting village that wins the fight costs nothing. Default: on.
{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryRaidOwnerAmount}Raid: Relation Lost With The Owner's Clan Leader

{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryRaidOwnerAmount_hint}Relation lost with the clan leader who owns the village after a whole raid, before the alignment multiplier. Vanilla takes its own share as well. Between 0 and 100. Default: 50.

{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryRaidNotableAmount_hint}Relation lost with every notable of the village after a whole raid, before the alignment multiplier. Vanilla takes its own share as well. Between 0 and 100. Default: 50.
{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryCoercionOwnerAmount}Forced Taking: Relation Lost With The Owner's Clan Leader

{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryCoercionOwnerAmount_hint}Relation lost with the clan leader who owns the village each time you force it to give goods or recruits, before the alignment multiplier. Between 0 and 50. Default: 20.
{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryCoercionNotableAmount}Forced Taking: Relation Lost With Each Notable

{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryCoercionNotableAmount_hint}Relation lost with every notable of the village each time you force it to give goods or recruits, before the alignment multiplier. Between 0 and 50. Default: 25.
{=taom_mcm_LongMemorySame_hint}Multiplier on the loss when you and the village owner's realm are on the same side, both Free or both Evil: the harshest pairing. Default: 1.00.
{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryNeutral_hint}Multiplier on the loss when you or the village owner's realm is on neither side. Default: 0.50.

{=taom_mcm_LongMemoryOpposite_hint}Multiplier on the loss when you and the village owner's realm are on opposite sides, such as an Evil warband raiding a Free village, where raiding is expected. Default: 0.10.

{=taom_mcm_EnableUnhappyCompanionTint_hint}On the Members tab of the clan screen, gives the row of a companion of your clan a faint red tint when their relation with you has fallen below zero, a warning before they leave. The age beside each child's name is always shown. Applies the next time the clan screen opens. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_PrisonerBannersEnabled_hint}On the party screen, a captive lord's row shows the clan's banner at the top left of the portrait, the kingdom's banner at the top right (when the clan belongs to a kingdom), and a gold noble icon at the bottom left when the lord leads the clan. Applies the next time the party screen opens. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_WardensTallyEnabled_hint}In the dungeon menu of a town or castle, adds under the engine's own line how many prisoners the dungeon holds against its capacity, how many of them are lords, each lord's chance to escape each day with the terms behind it (your clan holding him halves it; the governor's perks change it), and a line for a lord whose realm has a War of the Ring escape boost, or whom nothing lets escape. It only shows the odds the game already uses and changes no rule. Applies the next time the menu opens. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_SwornAnewEnabled_hint}When enabled (default), a captured lord can be asked to join your kingdom, in a conversation or from the party screen, and serves it instead of being ransomed. The lord must hold a clan of another kingdom (not its ruler, and not a mercenary or minor clan), must be held by your party or in a settlement your clan owns, and must not be a lord who can never be captured, such as Sauron and the Nazgul. A Free Peoples lord is never asked to join an Evil realm, and an Evil lord is never asked to join a Free one. The base game's blood feud rule still applies. When off, the base game's rules apply: only a kingdom's ruler can recruit a captured lord, through its 'join us, and be set free' line, which checks no realm. When on, both lines pass this check, and the ruler-only line also needs the lord held by your party or in your clan's dungeon. Applies at once, no restart.

{=taom_mcm_ProvenderEnabled_hint}Lets the hero you name Quartermaster (never you, and only while that hero is in your party) take standing orders in conversation: buy food at markets, slaughter livestock when the stores run low, lift the host's spirits with pay or drink, and sell your goods at a nearby town for a cut. Orders stand down for an enlisted player and for a co-op client. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_ProvenderLowFoodDays_hint}When the food in the stores, not counting the herd, lasts fewer days than this, the slaughter order turns livestock into meat, a head at a time, until it lasts this long again. Between 1 and 30. Default: 3.

{=taom_mcm_ProvenderKeepPerType_hint}The slaughter order always leaves this many head of each livestock type alive. The game itself still slaughters livestock when every other food is gone. Between 0 and 20. Default: 2.
{=taom_mcm_ProvenderSmallPayGold_hint}Gold paid to each soldier (not you) by the small pay option, in a settlement or a ready field camp. Between 10 and 500. Default: 50.
{=taom_mcm_ProvenderSmallPayMorale_hint}Morale the party gains from the small pay option. Between 1 and 30. Default: 5.
{=taom_mcm_ProvenderLargePayGold_hint}Gold paid to each soldier (not you) by the large pay option. Never read below the small pay's gold. Between 10 and 500. Default: 100.
{=taom_mcm_ProvenderLargePayMorale_hint}Morale the party gains from the large pay option. Never read below the small pay's morale. Between 1 and 30. Default: 10.

{=taom_mcm_ProvenderWageDaysKept_hint}The food order never spends the gold your party needs for this many days of wages, so buying food cannot leave your troops unpaid. 0 lets it spend the whole purse. Morale purchases are not limited: they show their price. Between 0 and 30. Default: 3.

{=taom_mcm_ProvenderSaleMaxFeePercent_hint}The Provender-master's cut, in percent of a town's price, when you send goods to be sold there and the Provender-master has no Trade skill. It falls to the smallest cut at Trade 250, and each town further down the list adds 5. Between 0 and 90. Default: 30.
{=taom_mcm_ProvenderSaleMinFeePercent_hint}The Provender-master's cut at Trade 250. Never read above the largest cut. Between 0 and 90. Default: 10.

{=taom_mcm_ProvenderSaleTownCount_hint}How many of the nearest towns that will buy from you the Provender-master offers. A town at war with you, of the opposing alignment, besieged, barring you or short of gold is never offered. Between 1 and 5. Default: 3.

{=taom_mcm_BondOfHireMinimumDays_hint}The fewest days a clan that signs on as a mercenary stays with its kingdom. Until then it cannot leave a ruler who is in debt, be hired away by another kingdom, or leave in its daily consideration of whether to stay. A clan with more time left is not shortened. Your own clan is not bound, and neither is dismissing or hiring away a mercenary yourself. 0 turns it off. Applies when a clan signs on; clans already serving get it at their next signing. Between 0 and 120. Default: 30.
{=taom_mercenary_menu_would_desert}These mercenaries would desert your party: their people will not serve your side.
{=taom_mercenary_refuses_your_side}Fight for your side? No coin buys that. Find your swords elsewhere.

{=taom_cleave_mcm_enable_hint}Your swings with a two-handed axe, mace, sword or polearm can cut through one enemy and strike the next. Each enemy after the first takes less damage. Armour slows the blade, and a kill or a clear skill lead over the victim carries it further. Cleaving Blows never applies to a shield block, a thrust or a swing from horseback. Only the character you control, unless the AI option below is on. Trolls and other big creatures keep their own cleave. The numbers live in combat_mechanics_config.json. Default: on.

{=taom_cleave_mcm_ai_hint}AI soldiers who swing a two-handed axe, mace or sword cut through enemies by the same rules. Every two-handed troop in both armies then hits a packed line harder. Needs Cleaving Blows on. Default: off.
{=taom_cleave_mcm_max_targets_hint}The most enemies one swing can strike, the first one included. Default 3. A swing often stops sooner: each enemy takes some of its force, and armour takes more.
{=taom_load_failed_body}An error occurred while this save loaded, and the game cannot continue the load. The error is in the TAOM log. Quit the game, then send that log with a bug report.
{=taom_mcm_ImeGuardEnabled}Pause the input method outside text fields

{=taom_mcm_ImeGuardEnabled_hint}For Chinese, Japanese and Korean input methods. While the game is in front and no text field has focus, the input method is paused, so hotkeys on the map and in battle reach the game instead of opening its candidate window. A search, rename or other text field gets it back at once, and other programs are not affected. Applies immediately. Default: on.

{=taom_stamina_mcm_enabled_hint}Experimental. In field battles, sieges and the Fords of War match soldiers have stamina. A melee swing, a shot, a throw, a jump, a kick, a shield bash and a blow stopped with a weapon or shield cost stamina, and running on foot drains it down to half. Stamina comes back while a soldier does not attack, more slowly while a block is held and not at all while running. A tired soldier swings and handles a weapon more slowly, and a tired AI soldier attacks less often. A soldier whose stamina reaches zero is exhausted until it is back at about a third: an exhausted soldier cannot attack, block, kick or jump, and on foot slows to a walk. Exceptions: a soldier who works a siege engine pays nothing and is not stopped, and a rider or a swimmer can still jump. Higher tier troops and heroes have more stamina. A soldier's people changes it too: Elves, Dwarves, Uruk-hai and trolls have more than most Men of the same rank, Orcs and goblins have less, and the Nazgul do not tire. Horses and other mounts are not affected. Takes effect from the next battle. Default: off.
{=taom_stamina_tired}You are tiring. Ease off before your strength fails.
{=taom_stamina_exhausted}Your strength fails you. Fall back and catch your breath.

{=taom_stamina_mcm_cost_scale_hint}Multiplies what every action costs in stamina, for every soldier: the player, allies and enemies alike. 0.50 halves the costs, 2.00 doubles them. It does not change how fast stamina comes back or how much a soldier has. Read at each battle tick. Default: 1.00.

{=taom_stamina_mcm_show_bar_hint}Shows your own stamina as a bar beside the battle HUD rings while Combat Stamina is on. The bar changes colour as you tire and turns grey while you are exhausted. Off hides the bar only: stamina still works. Drawn on this client only. Default: on.

{=taom_stamina_mcm_player_hint}When on, the soldier you control has stamina while Combat Stamina is on: your actions cost it and you can become exhausted. Off exempts that soldier: your stamina never drains, you are never stopped, and the stamina bar is hidden. AI soldiers still follow the next setting. Read at each battle tick. Default: on.

{=taom_stamina_mcm_ai_hint}When on, the soldiers the AI controls have stamina while Combat Stamina is on, allies and enemies alike. Off exempts them all: only the soldier you control tires, if the setting above is on. Read at each battle tick. Default: on.

{=taom_mcm_EnableBattleGearLoot_hint}When on, the loot from enemies your party beats in a battle your side wins is the gear they fought in: each weapon, armour piece, horse and harness drops on its own roll, at the chance below. It replaces the usual random loot from fallen enemies; captured baggage, gold, prisoners and renown are unchanged. Heavy, elite and lord armour held back by Armour Acquisition, named weapons and banners never drop. Singleplayer only: in a co-op session the usual loot applies. Default: off.

{=taom_mcm_BattleGearLootChancePercent_hint}The chance, from 0 to 100%, that each item of each beaten enemy drops. In a battle fought beside allies you loot your share of the enemies, as usual. Default: 10.

{=taom_mcm_CoopLoadOrderWarning}Warn players whose load order differs from the host's

{=taom_mcm_CoopLoadOrderWarning_hint}When a player joins a co-op campaign, the co-op server compares the order of TAOM and of every mod that adds items, troops or factions with its own, and tells a player whose order differs which two mods are the other way round. Nothing is blocked. The co-op server process reads this switch each time a player joins; a player's own value is not read. {=taom_mcm_CoopCareerSync_hint}When on, a career a co-op player picks or changes goes to the co-op server, which checks it with the career rules, keeps it in its save and shows it to the other players, so the career is still there after the player joins again. The co-op server process reads this switch each time a player reports a career; a player's own value is not read. A dedicated server takes it from taom-server-settings.json (CoopCareerSync), which it reads once at start, so change it there and restart the server. Off: each player's career stays only on that player's PC and is lost when the player joins again. Default: on.

The rung quests are not offered to co-op players. The co-op server process reads this switch each time a player uses an armoury or a battle ends; a player's own value is not read. A dedicated server takes it from taom-server-settings.json (CoopGuestLadder), which it reads once at start, so change it there and restart the server. Off: co-op players see no ladder at the armoury and find no new lord's materials after battles; materials already found are still given. Default: on.
